title: Delaunay Weighted Two-sample Test for High-dimensional Data by Incorporating Geometric Information
abstractText: Two-sample hypothesis testing is a fundamental problem with various applications, which faces new challenges in the high-dimensional context. To mitigate the issue of the curse of dimensionality, high-dimensional data are typically assumed to lie on a low-dimensional manifold. To incorporate geometric information in the data, we propose to apply the Delaunay triangulation and develop the Delaunay weight to measure the geometric proximity among data points. In contrast to existing similarity measures that only utilize pairwise distances, the Delaunay weight can take both the distance and direction information into account. A detailed computation procedure is developed to learn the unknown manifold and approximate the Delaunay weight. We further propose a novel nonparametric test statistic using the Delaunay weight matrix. Asymptotic normality under the null and consistency under the alternative of the test statistic are developed. Applied on simulated data, the new test shows robustness to the learning of the unknown manifold and exhibits substantial power gain if the distributions differ directions. The proposed test also shows great power on a real dataset of mice protein expression levels.

title: Energetic constraints reshape climate-tracking opportunities for large mammals across European protected-area networks
abstractText: Study overview Protected areas (PAs) remain central to biodiversity conservation, but climate change is shifting temperature conditions beyond the boundaries of many protected sites. Their effectiveness therefore increasingly depends on both the time for which analogous climatic conditions remain available within a PA and the potential for species to move through surrounding landscapes. Our study develops a climate-informed connectivity framework for 10,908 terrestrial PAs across Europe. It integrates temperature-based climate velocity, protected-area climatic residence time, current habitat suitability, physical and anthropogenic barriers, and terrain-related energetic movement costs. Functional connectivity is evaluated for ten focal large-mammal taxa, summarized into two analytical archetypes: large ungulates (the herbivore archetype) and large carnivores (the carnivore archetype). The framework identifies where climatic persistence and movement potential coincide, where they are spatially mismatched, and where climate-tracking opportunities may be constrained by both rapid climatic turnover and low landscape permeability.

title: Teachers' Perceptions About Head Teachers' Supervisory Role in Government Secondary Schools of Larkana
abstractText: This study provides a comprehensive view of the perceptions of teachers about the role head teachers plays at their schools in Larkana city. This quantitative research study will help head teachers to improve their skills and fill their gaps. This study focused on the teachers’ positive and negative perceptions about head teachers’ supervisory role, its impacts, effectiveness and challenges teachers face at their institutions under the supervision. The main objectives of the study are to investigate supervisory practices of head teachers at their schools, what perceptions teachers have built about the supervisory role of the head teachers and whether the supervisory role enhance their job satisfaction or not. This study adopted quantitative research approach and explanatory research design. The population of the study was government teachers of secondary schools from 30 schools of Larkana district, data was collected through online questionnaire administrated to 80 teachers included both male and female, and used simple random sampling technique to select the participants. The questionnaire was based on 30 items on the different supervisory role of head teacher and the collected data was analyzed through SPSS software version 23. The study provided quantified result about teachers’ perceptions regarding head teachers supervisory role and almost all the findings were between strongly agree and agree. The collected data shows that teachers of the Larkana district are very satisfied with the supervision role of their head teachers and the head teachers work ideally for their schools but here, the question is raised, then why the performance and results of the schools is not satisfactory. The teachers of the Larkana should reevaluate their head teachers.

title: Impact of Inclusive Leadership on Workplace Microaggressions and Building Fair Work Environment and Effective Mobilization of Inclusive Work Teams: A Study on DEIB Corporate Perspective
abstractText: The present study examined the influence of inclusive leadership on building fair work environments and effective mobilization of inclusive work teams through the mediating mechanism of workplace microaggressions. The study was theoretically anchored in the Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging (DEIB) framework and further supported by Leadership Theory, Social Exchange Theory, and Inclusion Theory. A quantitative research design was adopted within a positivist philosophical orientation using a deductive approach. Cross-sectional primary data were collected through a structured questionnaire from employees working in multinational food processing and manufacturing companies in Pakistan. A total of 492 valid responses were obtained through convenience sampling and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) through SmartPLS. The findings revealed that inclusive leadership significantly reduced workplace microaggressions while positively contributing to both fair work environment and effective mobilization of inclusive work teams. Workplace microaggressions demonstrated significant negative effects on organizational outcomes and partially mediated the relationship between inclusive leadership and both dependent variables. The results indicate that leadership-driven inclusion contributes to organizational effectiveness not only directly but also through minimizing subtle exclusionary experiences embedded within everyday workplace interactions. The study advances contemporary DEIB literature by providing an integrated explanation of how inclusive leadership influences employee experiences and organizational outcomes simultaneously. Practically, the findings suggest that organizations seeking sustainable inclusion should move beyond symbolic diversity initiatives and institutionalize leadership practices that strengthen belonging, fairness, and collaborative workforce engagement. The study offers strategic implications for multinational organizations operating in increasingly diverse and performance-oriented environments.

title: Intracavity THz Generation Using a Thin Lithium Niobate Plate in a Compact Kerr-Lens Mode-Locked Yb:CALGO Bulk Oscillator
abstractText: Abstract We demonstrate intracavity terahertz (THz) generation via optical rectification in a 50-µm-thick lithium niobate crystal placed inside a compact diode-pumped Kerr-lens mode-locked (KLM) Yb:CALGO bulk oscillator. The oscillator operates at a repetition rate of 85 MHz and delivers 83-fs pulses with up to 71 W of average intracavity power, obtained with only 21.4 W of low-cost multimode diode pump power. We generate single-cycle THz pulses with a spectrum extending up to 3 THz, detected by electro-optic sampling with 60-dB dynamic range within 156 s of measurement time (313 averaged traces) and up to 120 µW of THz average power. This work combines the high damage threshold, power-handling capability, and cost-effectiveness of thin-LN plates with simplicity, compactness, and low-cost multimode diode-pumped solid-state bulk lasers, offering an attractive alternative for high-repetition-rate THz time-domain spectroscopy systems.

title: Prevalence Of Transfusion-Transmissible Haemoparasites And Associated Disruptions In Serum Iron Profile Among Blood Donors In Ibadan, Nigeria
abstractText: ABSTRACTBlood transfusion safety in sub-Saharan Africa remains compromised by transfusion-transmissible haemoparasites that fall outside routine mandatory donor screening. This study evaluated the prevalence of malaria parasitaemia and microfilaraemia among prospective blood donors and examined associated alterations in serum iron and transferrin at the Blood Bank, University College Hospital (UCH), Ibadan, Nigeria. In a descriptive cross-sectional study, 300 apparently healthy prospective donors were recruited using a structured questionnaire. Thick and thin blood films stained with Giemsa were examined for malaria parasites, and Knott's concentration technique was used to detect microfilariae. Serum iron and transferrin were quantified by colorimetric and immunoturbidimetric assay, respectively, on the Roche/Hitachi Cobas C system. Malaria parasitaemia was detected in 51 donors (17.0%) and microfilariae in 4 donors (1.3%); no trypanosomes were identified. Mean serum iron was significantly lower in malaria-positive donors (10.3±3.4 μmol/L) than malaria-negative donors (14.3±4.8 μmol/L, p<0.001), and in microfilaria-positive donors (12.5±0.37 μmol/L) than microfilaria-negative donors (13.6±4.9 μmol/L, p=0.004). Serum transferrin was significantly lower in malaria-positive donors (2.15±0.27 g/L) than malaria-negative donors (2.35±0.77 g/L, p<0.001) but did not differ significantly by microfilaria status. Abnormal serum iron was significantly associated with malaria positivity (χ²=14.400, p<0.001) but not with microfilaria status. These findings demonstrate that occult haemoparasitaemia among asymptomatic blood donors is associated with measurable derangement of iron homeostasis, with implications for donor health and recipient safety. Routine malaria screening should be considered within donor selection algorithms in malaria- endemic transfusion settings.

title: Разработка подхода к комплексной оценке состояния нарушенных земель горными работами
abstractText: Large-scale mineral mining, including critical minerals of oil, gas and coal, conditions withdrawal of vast land from the agricultural sector. The relevance of this problem is connected with prevention and elimination of disamenity of the subsoil use. It is necessary to determine a strategy of mining-disturbed land reclamation. The authors propose an integrated assessment of mining-disturbed land, which allows a comprehensive analysis of current condition of these man-made sites. The proposed procedure can serve as a framework for the development of recommendations on reclamation trend selection. It enables simultaneous sequential or parallel application of parameters and criteria from a compiled list. In the aggregate, these parameters and criteria describe features of man-made objects and their condition by quantitative and qualitative indicators determined during field study, field survey, lab-scale testing and office analysis. As a case study of the Novosibirsk Region, the necessity is demonstrated and a matrix is constructed for the mining-disturbed land assessment by the level and nature of the environmental impact, with the determination of boundaries and sizes of damage areas. The basis for ranking man-made objects was classification, typification and clustering of attributes which govern peculiarities of the external impacts on the environment (rocks, soil, artificial ground, surface water, groundwater, etc.). These attributes are characterized by parameters and quantitative indicators measured on various scales, which identify admissible and hyperadmissible environmental load. The proposed approach allows the integrated analysis of mining-disturbed land areas with a view to their further ranking by the environmental load, and for developing an expert system of the optimized selection of new application ranges for such land.

title: Job Related Push Factors and Brain Drain Intention among Gen Z Employees in Pakistan
abstractText: Brain drain is a growing concern for developing economies because the migration of skilled employees weakens organisational capability, innovation and economic development. This study examined how workplace-related push factors influence brain-drain intention among Generation Z employees in Pakistan’s information technology sector. The primary aim of this study is to examine the impact of job-related push factors on brain drain intention among Generation Z employees in Pakistan’s IT sector. Specifically, the study seeks to analyse how factors such as restricted career growth, incentive programs, work-life balance, organisational support, and learning opportunities influence employees’ intention to seek employment abroad. Quantitative cross-sectional research was conducted. The data for the study was collected from a survey among 206 Gen Z information technology employees using a 5-point Likert scale. Restrictive factors involved in the study include career development, incentives, work-life balance problems, perception of organisational support, developmental opportunities, and brain-drain intentions. The data analysis using SPSS involved descriptive analysis, Cronbach's alpha, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis. Scales proved to be reliable as their values for Cronbach's alpha were .944-.964. Brain-drain intentions were rather high (M = 4.01). Restricted career development and work-life balance problems had a positive significant impact on brain-drain intentions, while incentive programs, organisational support perception, and development opportunities had a negative one. Work-life balance problems had the highest predictive value. The regression model accounted for 64.9% of the variance in brain-drain intentions. The working environment determines the migration intentions of Generation Z IT employees. Organisations need to give priority to such aspects as work-life balance, career prospects, proper incentives, supportive management and development.

title: Between Aspiration and Infrastructure: The Opportunity-Reality Divergence in STEM Teacher Education in Karachi, Pakistan
abstractText: A foundational assumption in applying Ajzen's Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to STEM teacher education is that prospective teachers' perceived behavioural control reflects the actual enabling conditions of their institutional environment. This study tests that assumption empirically in the context of STEM integration in Karachi, Pakistan, one of the most understudied urban teacher education landscapes in South Asia. Using an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, we surveyed 310 prospective teachers and interviewed 15 teacher educators. Findings reveal that while prospective teachers held strongly positive perceptions of integrated STEM education and available opportunities, teacher educators consistently reported that actual STEM infrastructure, such as laboratories, digital tools, and interdisciplinary planning time, is substantially more limited. Furthermore, knowledge of STEM education emerged as the strongest predictor of positive perceptions, with self-efficacy and behavioural intentions also making significant contributions. Ultimately, the study identifies a systematic opportunity-reality divergence in which prospective teachers overestimate institutional support. This pattern reframes the local policy problem: the barrier to STEM implementation in Pakistan is not insufficient teacher motivation, but the structural absence of the enabling conditions that motivated teachers assume exist.

title: Unusual Lateral Presentation of Thyroglossal Duct Cyst in a 30 Year Old Male: A Case Report
abstractText: Background: Thyroglossal duct cyst (TGDC) is the most common congenital anterior neck mass, typically presenting in the paediatric age group as a painless midline swelling. The diagnosis is primarily clinical, supported by imaging modalities and fine needle aspiration cytology for confirmation and exclusion of other pathologies. Classically, TGDC presents as a midline neck swelling that moves with deglutition and tongue protrusion; however, atypical presentations can cause diagnostic uncertainty. Case Presentation: In this case report, we describe an atypical presentation of thyroglossal duct cyst in an adult patient presenting with lateral neck swelling. The case highlights the importance of considering TGDC in the differential diagnosis of lateral neck masses and emphasizes the role of detailed preoperative assessment. The patient was successfully managed with surgical excision using the Sistrunk procedure, with favourable outcome. Conclusion: Though TGDC may occur at any age, a newly appearing lateral neck mass in adults warrants careful evaluation to exclude neoplastic causes. Rarely, TGDC may present in an unusual location or with acute onset due to infection or rapid enlargement.

title: Применение материала из бедных вермикулит-серпентиновых руд для рекультивации городских почв и агропочв в Арктической зоне России
abstractText: The problem of waste disposal in the mining industry is urgent for the Arctic zone of Russia. Significant volumes of overburden rocks from the Kovdor phlogopite deposit, represented by poor vermiculite-sungulite ores, require the development of environmentally safe methods for their integration into economic circulation. The aim of the study is to assess the potential of vermiculite-serpentine concentrate (VSC) obtained from overburden rocks for the remediation of anthropogenically disturbed soils. The prospect of using VSC for improving soil properties is due to its favourable mineral composition (serpentine 30-35, vermiculite 28-31 wt.%). Laboratory experiments prepared mixtures of VSC with agrosoil (10-60 wt.%) and samples of urban soils from three cities in the Murmansk Region (Apatity, Kirovsk, and Monchegorsk) (20 wt.%), differing in the level of anthropogenic impact. The content of chemical elements in two mobile fractions was studied, phytotesting was carried out with French marigolds (Tagetes patula). VSC has an alkaline reaction (рНН2О 8.9) due to the presence of minerals in the composition capable of concentrating Ni; the gross content of this component is 730 mg/kg. It was found that the introduction of VSC increases the alkalinity of soil mixtures and the content of mobile forms of Ca and Mg. In slightly contaminated agrosoil, the content of mobile nickel when adding 10-50 % VSC increases from 1.5 to 2.5 mg/kg, with a content of more than 60 % it decreases below background values. Phytotesting showed that in the range of 10-60 % VSC, the root mass increased from 0.09-0.1 to 0.13-0.18 g/plant, there were no signs of phytotoxicity. For soils of Monchegorsk, characterized by a high level of anthropogenic contamination with nickel and copper, the introduction of concentrate, on the contrary, led to a steady decrease in the content of mobile forms of both metals. Vermiculite-serpentine concentrate can be recommended as a meliorant for soil remediation, poor in macroelements and contaminated with heavy metals.

title: Комплексная ресурсно-экологическая оценка возможности утилизации техногенных отходов
abstractText: The study presents analysis of the properties and parameters of waste from high-temperature processing of mineral raw materials – blast-furnace and steelmaking slags, dump slags from copper smelting and ferrochrome production, and incinerator slag. We perform a detailed analysis of the material composition of the studied materials, identify key resource and environmentally significant indicators of the chemical composition and physical properties of the waste, and adopt these as indicators of the resource and environmental potential of the slags. The paper considers approaches to grouping raw materials of industrial origin into categories with similar resource value and environmental hazard. As an alternative for classifying waste from high-temperature processes, we propose a cluster-based approach that enables building a categorization system for industrial raw materials according to their properties and limiting the number of sampling features while maintaining sufficient coverage of the classified materials. After standardizing and checking the multicollinearity of the selected indicators of the slags’ resource and environmental potential in the analysed dataset, the study finds that most indicators show low, absent, or random correlation. Using the Statistica software, we rank the studied materials via fuzzy clustering. Based on the resulting distribution, we define three cluster groups for treatment: resource-inert; resource-valuable with moderate environmental impact; and environmentally hazardous, requiring deep processing. The results show that granulated blast-furnace slags, lump blast-furnace slag, and ferrochrome production slag are suitable for manufacturing construction materials without preliminary dressing, provided the products meet environmental safety requirements. Steelmaking slags represent a resource-valuable material with moderate environmental impact and are suitable for producing metal concentrate. Copper-bearing slags and incinerator slags are environmentally hazardous and require deep processing with metal recovery, while tailings need stabilization and neutralization. The obtained results form the basis for further development of a methodology for comprehensive resource and environmental assessment of industrial mineral facilities, which is necessary for transitioning to closed-loop production cycles.

abstractText: Initially, anionic (SDS) and cationic (TBAB) micelles were prepared with a suitable concentration (0.1 mM) in potassium phosphate buffer at physiological conditions (pH=7.4 and T=37◦C). This matter was encouraged on complete assessment of the equilibrium state between chemotherapy compound (5-FU) with micelles, which it can be accompanied into formation processes of molecular complexes. title: GAN-Enhanced Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening: A Comprehensive Survey
abstractText: Abstract Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by difficulties in social communication and interaction, together with restricted or repetitive patterns of behavior. Early screening is important for facilitating timely clinical assessment and intervention; however, conventional screening approaches often depend on clinical expertise, behavioral observation, developmental history, and standardized assessment tools. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have created new opportunities for data-driven and automated ASD screening. This survey provides a comprehensive review of AI-based approaches for ASD screening, with particular emphasis on multimodal learning and the integration of heterogeneous data sources. Behavioral, genetic, environmental, neuroimaging, physiological, and clinical data modalities are examined, along with approaches for combining information across multiple sources. The survey further reviews the role of GANs and related generative approaches in synthetic-data generation and data augmentation, particularly in addressing challenges associated with limited and imbalanced datasets. Multimodal fusion strategies, multi-input neural networks, and emerging deep learning approaches are also discussed in the context of ASD screening. The reviewed literature indicates that multimodal AI has the potential to provide a more comprehensive representation of ASD-related characteristics than single-modality approaches. However, important challenges remain, including limited and heterogeneous datasets, class imbalance, multimodal data integration, GAN training instability, synthetic-data quality, privacy and security, model interpretability, generalizability, and limited external clinical validation. This survey identifies these challenges and highlights research directions toward reliable, explainable, privacy-preserving, and clinically validated AI-based multimodal ASD screening systems. Keywords: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD); Artificial Intelligence; Machine Learning; Deep Learning; Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs); Multimodal Learning; ASD Screening; Data Augmentation; Synthetic Data

title: From Ratings to Sensors: Real-Time AIIoT-Based Credibility Anchored on Blockchain for Ride-Sharing Ecosystems
abstractText: Current ride-sharing platforms predominantly rely on subjective post-ride ratings to evaluate driver credibility, making reputation systems vulnerable to user bias, delayed feedback, collusion, and manipulation. Although recent studies have explored blockchain-based ride-sharing, AI-driven driver monitoring, and IoT-enabled transportation independently, they do not provide an integrated trust framework that continuously derives credibility from objectively verifiable driving behaviour while maintaining scalability and low operational cost.This paper presents Ridezy, a decentralized trust architecture that replaces conventional rating-based reputation with real-time sensor-driven credibility. The proposed framework combines edge Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things (AIIoT) technologies to continuously monitor behavioural indicators such as lane discipline, speed compliance, braking behaviour, and traffic sign adherence. Instead of storing high-frequency telemetry on the blockchain, Ridezy employs a hybrid architecture in which behavioural summaries are processed off-chain and only cryptographic hashes, credibility updates, and payment records are anchored on Polygon smart contracts, enabling tamper-evident trust with minimal blockchain overhead. To evaluate the proposed architecture, Ridezy is compared against three representative trust models: a traditional rating-based system, an AI-only architecture, and a blockchain-only architecture. The evaluation considers behavioural detection performance, end-to-end latency, cost efficiency, throughput, reputation stability, tamper resistance, and component-wise ablation studies. Experimental results demonstrate that the hybrid architecture achieves higher behavioural fidelity and stronger trust guarantees than conventional reputation mechanisms while maintaining low per-ride blockchain cost and scalable operation through batched on-chain commitments.The primary contribution of this work is a sensor-driven credibility framework that transforms real-time behavioural evidence into a cryptographically verifiable trust primitive for ride-sharing ecosystems. By combining edge AI, IoT telemetry, and blockchain-based trust anchoring within a scalable hybrid architecture, Ridezy provides a practical foundation for trustworthy, transparent, and next-generation intelligent mobility systems.

title: A Comparative Study of QAOA and Classical Metaheuristics for Inventory Optimization
abstractText: We investigate whether the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can compete with classical metaheuristics for multi-product, multi-location retail inventory optimization under demand uncertainty. We formulate the binary inventory decision problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model and benchmark QAOA (simulated via classical statevector simulation, $p=2$ layers) against Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP), Simulated Annealing (SA), Genetic Algorithms (GA), and Tabu Search across problem sizes from $n=5$ to $n=200$ binary variables, using Walmart sales and Kaggle retail demand datasets. Our key finding is a \textbf{negative result}: while QAOA achieves a 2.3\% optimality gap and 97\% constraint satisfaction at small scales ($n \leq 20$), it is not competitive with classical metaheuristics at practical problem sizes. Classical heuristics---particularly SA and Tabu Search---consistently outperform QAOA on all instances tested and scale efficiently to $n=200$, whereas QAOA simulation becomes intractable beyond $n=30$ due to exponential memory requirements. We do not claim any quantum speedup. This comparative study provides important insights into the limitations of current QAOA implementations for supply chain problems, including the effects of penalty parameter scaling, barren plateaus in the optimization landscape, and circuit depth constraints. We additionally present an economic sensitivity analysis linking macroeconomic indicators to optimal inventory decisions and a rolling-horizon proof-of-concept for multi-period planning.

title: Distinguishing Insomnia from Sleep Apnea Using Demographic, Lifestyle, and Physiological Variables: A Secondary Analysis with Deduplication and Occupational Confounding
abstractText: Insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) are the two most common sleep disorders in the world, however, data on the routine assessment of lifestyle and physiology is rarely utilized to differentiate between the two sleep disorders. A publicly available secondary data set was used to investigate if demographic, lifestyle and physiological factors can distinguish participants with insomnia from those with sleep apnea. Sleep Health and Lifestyle Dataset (n = 374 records) were used to obtain data. The simple screening of the records identified 320 of 374 records (85.6\%) as exact duplicates, and 132 (73\%) profiles remained after the deduplication process (73 with no disorder, 29 with insomnia, and 30 with sleep apnea). To quantify the consequence of this duplication, the accuracy of classification was calculated on the pre-registered file, before and after deduplication, and the results were found to be 90.9\% (\(\pm\)4.1\%) and 71.9\% (\(\pm\)13.0\%), respectively. This was a pre-registered sensitivity analysis that confirmed classification accuracy on the file after deduplication was a spurious, over-estimated performance metric, and that deduplication was an essential step in the process, not something that could be neglected as just an incidental. One way ANOVA, the Kruskal-Wallis test and the chi-square test were used to assess group differences, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons and effect sizes (\(\eta^2\) and Cramér's V) reported; all nine continuous variables and both categorical variables remained significant after correction. To compare three classifiers, multinomial logistic regression, a random forest and gradient boosting-nested stratified 5-fold cross validation with hyperparameter tuning was employed for three-class sleep-disorder prediction. A variance-inflation-factor-screened multivariable logistic regression was used to develop odds ratios that discriminated insomnia from sleep apnea in the disorder-only subsample (n = 59) using a dedicated binary model (logistic regression and RF). All the variables tested were different among the three groups at all levels (p < 0.05). The three-class logistic regression model obtained a nested cross-validated accuracy of 71.1\% (\(\pm\)15.6\%; macro-F1 = 0.62) for cross validation. The binary insomnia vs sleep apnea model had a nested cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.74 (\(\pm\)0.13). Nursing occupation, which was significantly over-represented among sleep apnea cases compared to insomnia cases (56.7\% vs. 10.3\%, \(\chi^2\) = 12.1, p < 0.001), explained most of the association with physical activity level (OR = 3.97 for each 1 SD increase; 95\% CI, 1.34-11.83; p = 0.013), and in a parsimonious model that included nursing occupation, physical activity remained not significant (OR = 1.74, p = 0.17) while nursing occupation was (OR = 6.95, 95\% CI 1.40-34.6, p = 0.018). The present data should be viewed as hypothesis-generating and the ability to distinguish insomnia phenotypes from sleep apnea phenotypes was modest even when controlling for occupation, indicating that other variables that are routinely collected showed less promise of distinguishing these phenotypes. We conclude that lifestyle and physiological-based screening strategies capable of screening in a few minutes are a viable path forward for future research, but should be validated in larger, prospective, occupation-balanced and clinically confirmed cohorts before any evidence for clinical utility can be established.

title: A Due Diligence Study on the Factors That Matter For Successful Implementation of Metro Rail Projects from Indian Context
abstractText: The successful implementation of metro rail projects is essential for supporting sustainable urban mobility, economic growth, and infrastructure development in India. This study identifies and prioritizes the critical success factors influencing metro rail project implementation from the Indian perspective. A structured questionnaire survey was administered using a simple random sampling technique, yielding 139 valid responses from 150 distributed questionnaires. The collected data were analysed using percentage analysis, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA), correlation analysis, regression analysis, and the Relative Importance Index (RII). The findings reveal that infrastructure-related challenges ranked as the most critical factor (RII = 0.547), followed by rolling stock-related challenges (RII = 0.519) and signalling and control-related challenges (RII = 0.517). The regression analysis further indicates that effective management of critical success factors is positively associated with improved project profitability and reduced project timelines. The study provides practical recommendations for policymakers, project managers, engineers, and legal teams to enhance governance, technical execution, risk management, and stakeholder coordination. Although the findings offer valuable insights for metro rail projects in India, their applicability may vary across other infrastructure sectors and geographical contexts, warranting further validation through comparative international studies.

title: Machine Learning-Based Customer Lifetime Value Prediction in E-Commerce: A Comparative Study of Regression, Ensemble and Neural Models
abstractText: Customer lifetime value (CLV) is useful only when an organization can turn transaction history into a credible estimate of future customer worth. This study develops a customer-level CLV prediction pipeline from 17,049 e-commerce transaction records representing 5,000 customers observed from January 2023 to February 2024. Transactional data were aggregated and transformed into 33 modelling attributes, including recency, tenure, purchase frequency, average order value and discount-related measures, together with encoded demographic and behavioural variables. Four regression approaches---ridge-based Linear Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosted Trees and a feed-forward Neural Network---were examined in Altair AI Studio (RapidMiner) using a common 10-fold cross-validation design. The model comparison is based primarily on the common cross-validation stream, while predictions exported for all 5,000 customer records are reported separately as scoring diagnostics because the two evaluation paths are not equivalent for every learner. The exported prediction files produced RMSE values of 2,289.58, 2,053.98, 1,363.53 and 297.06, respectively. The Neural Network achieved MAE=187.86, $R^2$=0.9968 and correlation=0.9984 on those exported outputs. Beyond model ranking, the study converts predicted customer value into three actionable segments: 2,763 low-value, 1,252 medium-value and 985 high-value customers. The results also show that evaluation provenance, temporal separation of predictors and target, and non-negative prediction constraints are essential when highly accurate scoring outputs are interpreted for deployment. The paper therefore links predictive accuracy with practical customer portfolio decisions rather than treating CLV as a purely statistical exercise.

title: Synthesis, Spectroscopic Characterization, and Antibacterial Evaluation of Selected Aryl-Substituted Pyrrolidine and Morpholine Derivatives
abstractText: Five selected arylated tertiary amines of the pyrrolidine and morpholine series were prepared from para-substituted aryl bromides and the corresponding cyclic secondary amines in DMSO/NaOH under reflux. The products N1--N5 were isolated in 58--70\% yield and assessed by melting-point determination, FTIR, and $^1$H/$^{13}$C NMR spectroscopy. The spectra differentiated the aldehyde, acetyl, nitro, aromatic, and cyclic-amine features; because molecular-ion and elemental-composition data were not available, the assignments are regarded as first-line structural characterization. Antibacterial activity was screened by agar-well diffusion against \emph{Escherichia coli} and \emph{Staphylococcus aureus} using 100~$\mu$L aliquots that delivered 10, 5, or 2.5~mg per well. DMSO served as the negative control. N2 produced the largest zones at 10~mg/well (23~mm against \emph{E. coli} and 17~mm against \emph{S. aureus}), followed by N5 (16 and 12~mm). N4 showed weaker inhibition, N3 produced only weak inhibition of \emph{S. aureus}, and N1 was inactive. Because no positive-antibiotic control, replicate-based statistical analysis, MIC determination, or cytotoxicity assessment was included, the biological findings are interpreted as preliminary screening data.

title: Physical Constraints in Molecular Communication: 2D Diffusion in Stiff and Crowded Hydrogels
abstractText: Diffusion is a fundamental process that governs molecular transport in biological systems and is influenced by the physical and chemical properties of the surrounding environment, including matrix stiffness and molecular crowding. In this study, we developed a two-dimensional hydrogel-based model to investigate how these factors modulate diffusion. Two concentrations of agarose gels (\(1\%\) w/v and \(2\%\) w/v) were taken to represent differences in matrix stiffness, while \(10\%\) w/v sucrose was introduced to create a crowding effect in respective conditions. In our setup, four experimental conditions were designed and analysed, i.e. baseline condition A (\(1\%\) w/v agarose), condition B (\(1\%\) w/v agarose with \(10\%\) w/v sucrose), condition C (\(2\%\) w/v agarose), and condition D (\(2\%\) w/v agarose with \(10\%\) w/v sucrose). Diffusion of methylene blue in four hydrogel conditions was monitored for over 24 hours, and radial spread of dye was quantified by image analysis using ImageJ. The mean squared radius (\(r^2\)) followed a linear relationship with time across all conditions in agreement with Fickian diffusion. However, effective diffusion was progressively reduced from baseline to respective conditions (A \(>\) B \(>\) C \(>\) D), with a percentage reduction of \(6.9\%\) on introducing crowding in condition B, \(14.5\%\) under stiffness alone in condition C and \(21.8\%\) under combined constraints in condition D at a significance level of \(p < 0.05\). These observations and results indicate that stiffness and crowding have an independent and additive effect on restricting molecular transport. This model provides a simple framework for understanding how physical limitations can influence diffusion-driven processes in complex biological environments.

title: Gene Therapy Knowledge Among Nursing Students in Chengalpattu: A Mathematical Modeling Study
abstractText: Gene therapy represents a paradigm shift in modern medicine, offering potential cures for previously untreatable genetic disorders. Despite its growing clinical relevance and increasing integration into healthcare systems, knowledge of gene therapy among future healthcare professionals remains inadequately characterized. This study aimed to (1) assess the level of knowledge regarding gene therapy among B.Sc. Nursing students; (2) examine the association between knowledge level and selected demographic variables; (3) identify specific knowledge gaps in gene therapy concepts; and (4) develop a mathematical model to predict knowledge levels based on demographic characteristics. A quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 320 B.Sc. Nursing students at Bhaarath College of Nursing, Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research, Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu, using a non-probability convenience sampling technique. Data were collected using a 30-item semi-structured knowledge questionnaire. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, binary logistic regression, and Item Response Theory (IRT) analysis, with significance set at $p < 0.05$. Knowledge assessment revealed that 132 participants (41.25\%) demonstrated inadequate knowledge, 100 (31.25\%) had moderate knowledge, and only 88 (27.50\%) showed adequate knowledge (mean score = 15.84 $\pm$ 6.39). IRT analysis revealed that items on CRISPR technology (difficulty: $b = 2.10$) and vector mechanisms (difficulty: $b = 1.76$) were the most challenging. Chi-square analysis indicated significant associations with gender ($\chi^2 = 16.64$, $p < 0.001$, Cram\'er's $V = 0.228$) and year of study ($\chi^2 = 21.70$, $p = 0.001$, Cram\'er's $V = 0.185$). Binary logistic regression identified year of study as the strongest predictor of adequate knowledge (OR = 2.14, 95\% CI: 1.38-3.31, $p < 0.001$). The predictive model achieved 72.8\% classification accuracy. The majority of B.Sc. Nursing students possess inadequate knowledge of gene therapy. Significant associations with gender and year of study suggest that educational interventions tailored to specific demographic groups could effectively address these knowledge gaps. The identified deficits in CRISPR and vector-related knowledge provide targeted areas for curriculum enhancement.

title: K-Means Clustering of Arrival Estimates in a 2D Signal Using DCONVNET
abstractText: This research presents a fast two-dimensional direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation approach based on a deep learning convolutional neural network (DCONVNET) for low-elevation targets of very-high-frequency (VHF) array radar. Initially, the technique uses the azimuth and pitch angle uncoupling properties of a uniform planar array to transform the two-dimensional angle estimation problem into two one-dimensional DOA estimation problems. Digital beamforming is used to retrieve the target information in the azimuth and elevation dimensions. Finally, the azimuth and pitch angles are estimated using the alternating direction method of multipliers. This approach significantly reduces complexity and eliminates the need for eigenvalue decomposition during operation, which further enhances efficiency by avoiding complicated two-dimensional joint estimation computation.

title: Photocatalytic Efficiency and Environmental Safety Assessment of Graphene Oxide for Sustainable Wastewater Treatment
abstractText: Graphene oxide (GO) has emerged as a promising nanomaterial for sustainable wastewater treatment because of its unique physicochemical properties and photocatalytic activity. In the present study, graphene oxide was synthesized using the modified Hummers' method and characterized by UV--Visible Spectroscopy, Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray Diffraction (XRD), confirming the successful formation of graphene oxide with characteristic structural and functional properties. The photocatalytic performance of the synthesized material was evaluated using crystal violet dye under natural sunlight, achieving gradual degradation within 45 minutes, demonstrating its potential for efficient pollutant removal. To assess the environmental safety of the treated wastewater, phytotoxicity studies were conducted using \textit{Vigna radiata}, which showed 99\% seed germination along with improved root and shoot growth compared with untreated samples. Cytotoxicity evaluation using the \textit{Allium cepa} root tip assay revealed 95.8\% similarity with the control, indicating negligible toxic effects after treatment. The combined results demonstrate that graphene oxide not only effectively degrades dye pollutants but also produces treated water that is environmentally compatible and biologically safe. This integrated assessment of material characterization, photocatalytic efficiency, phytotoxicity, and cytotoxicity provides comprehensive evidence supporting the application of graphene oxide as an eco-friendly and sustainable nanomaterial for wastewater treatment.

title: FedTrust-GNN: Federated Learning with Blockchain Trust and Graph Neural Networks for Decentralized Modeling
abstractText: Centralized user modeling systems inherently violate privacy regulations, with catastrophic failure points, opaque trust management mechanisms, and vulnerability to complex adversarial strategies such as poisoning attacks, model inversions, and membership inference. Federated learning (FL) approaches address data privacy issues by training models without centralized data storage. However, they suffer from Byzantine failures, lack of transparent reputation-based trust mechanisms, and inability to harness relational information implicit in user interactions. This paper proposes FedTrust-GNN, a secure and relationally aware decentralized user modeling framework that integrates federated learning, permissioned blockchain, and graph neural networks. The framework employs differentially private federated learning with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to perform gradient aggregation while providing strong privacy guarantees. A permissioned blockchain using the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) consensus protocol maintains an immutable ledger of participant behaviors, model contributions, and reputation scores, eliminating reliance on a trusted central authority. To model participant relationships, a heterogeneous graph attention network (HGAT) infers dynamic trust scores by capturing multihop trust propagation, collusion patterns, and evolving reputation through attention-based message passing. These trust scores guide a trust-weighted robust aggregation (TWRA) mechanism that combines norm clipping with coordinate-wise median aggregation, achieving Byzantine fault tolerance against up to 30\% malicious participants. title: Synthesis, Spectroscopic Characterization, and Antibacterial Evaluation of Selected Aryl-Substituted Pyrrolidine and Morpholine Derivatives
abstractText: Five selected arylated tertiary amines of the pyrrolidine and morpholine series were prepared from para-substituted aryl bromides and the corresponding cyclic secondary amines in DMSO/NaOH under reflux. The products N1--N5 were isolated in 58--70\% yield and assessed by melting-point determination, FTIR, and $^1$H/$^{13}$C NMR spectroscopy. title: K-Means Clustering of Arrival Estimates in a 2D Signal Using DCONVNET
abstractText: This research presents a fast two-dimensional direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation approach based on a deep learning convolutional neural network (DCONVNET) for low-elevation targets of very-high-frequency (VHF) array radar. Initially, the technique uses the azimuth and pitch angle uncoupling properties of a uniform planar array to transform the two-dimensional angle estimation problem into two one-dimensional DOA estimation problems. Digital beamforming is used to retrieve the target information in the azimuth and elevation dimensions. Finally, the azimuth and pitch angles are estimated using the alternating direction method of multipliers. This approach significantly reduces complexity and eliminates the need for eigenvalue decomposition during operation, which further enhances efficiency by avoiding complicated two-dimensional joint estimation computation.

title: Photocatalytic Efficiency and Environmental Safety Assessment of Graphene Oxide for Sustainable Wastewater Treatment
abstractText: Graphene oxide (GO) has emerged as a promising nanomaterial for sustainable wastewater treatment because of its unique physicochemical properties and photocatalytic activity. Cytotoxicity evaluation using the \textit{Allium cepa} root tip assay revealed 95.8\% similarity with the control, indicating negligible toxic effects after treatment. title: A System Dynamics-Based Multi-Objective Optimisation Framework for Interstate Reservoir Operations: Evidence from the Parambikulam--Aliyar Project, India
abstractText: Interstate reservoir systems require operating policies that balance water-supply reliability, flood-risk mitigation, hydropower generation, and operational stability under competing stakeholder demands and hydrological uncertainty. Conventional reservoir operation methods often fail to represent the dynamic interactions and trade-offs inherent in multi-reservoir systems. This study presents a System Dynamics (SD)-based multi-objective optimisation framework for interstate reservoir operations, demonstrated using the Parambikulam Aliyar Project (PAP), India. The proposed framework integrates a monthly SD simulation model with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to optimise storage-dependent, seasonally varying operating policies. A calibrated lumped-loss formulation is incorporated to represent aggregate operational losses, while four objectives are simultaneously considered: minimisation of water-supply deficits, minimisation of flood-risk exposure, maximisation of a planning-scale hydropower proxy, and minimisation of release variability. Model calibration and validation demonstrated satisfactory agreement between simulated and observed reservoir behaviour, confirming the reliability of the proposed simulation framework. The optimisation generated diverse Pareto-optimal operating policies representing reliability-oriented, flood-averse, and balanced operational strategies, thereby explicitly revealing trade-offs among the competing objectives. The balanced policy achieved an effective compromise between water-supply reliability, flood-risk reduction, hydropower potential, and operational smoothness, providing flexible decision support for different management priorities. The proposed SD-NSGA-II framework offers a transparent, computationally efficient, and operationally interpretable decision-support tool for planning-scale management of complex interstate reservoir systems and can be readily adapted to other multi-reservoir river basins.

title: IoT-AI Framework for Smart Reverse Osmosis Water Purification and Distribution
abstractText: This paper presents an IoT-enabled multi-sensor monitoring framework with AI-based predictive analytics for smart reverse osmosis (RO) water purification and distribution systems. The proposed architecture integrates six flow sensors (FS1--FS6) and two temperature sensors (T1--T2) with an ESP32-based embedded platform for continuous telemetry collection and cloud-based analytics. The predictive framework comprises: (1) RO purification efficiency estimation via inlet/outlet flow ratio modeling; (2) leakage detection using mass-balance water accounting; (3) system stability assessment via rolling standard deviation; and (4) water demand forecasting using linear regression and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks. Experimental validation using 31,450 real-world measurements demonstrates that the LSTM model achieves superior performance (R² = 0.94, RMSE = 245 L/min) compared to linear regression (R² = 0.72, RMSE = 520 L/min). The Isolation Forest-based anomaly detection algorithm achieves 95.7\% precision in identifying distribution anomalies. The integrated framework provides a practical solution for decentralized water infrastructure management in semi-urban and institutional settings.

title: A Novel Information-Theoretic Measure for Feature Selection in High-Dimensional Data
abstractText: Feature selection in high-dimensional machine learning is challenged by the curse of dimensionality, feature redundancy, and classifier instability. title: Clinical and Haematological Study on the Effects of Coccidiosis in Adult Sheep Presented to a Private Veterinary Clinic in Tikrit, Salah Al-Din Governorate, Iraq
abstractText: Coccidiosis caused by Eimeria spp. is commonly regarded as a disease of young lambs; however, adult sheep may also develop clinically significant infection under conditions of stress, poor husbandry, concurrent disease, or immunosuppression. This study evaluated the clinical and hematological effects of naturally occurring coccidiosis in adult sheep presented to a private veterinary clinic in Tikrit, Salah Al-Din Governorate, Iraq. A cross-sectional study was conducted on 100 adult sheep (\(>12\) months), comprising 50 clinically affected and Eimeria-positive sheep and 50 clinically healthy, Eimeria-negative controls. Fecal samples were examined using direct smear and McMaster flotation techniques to determine oocysts per gram (OPG), while an Eimeria coproantigen ELISA was used for confirmation. Complete blood counts and differential leukocyte counts were performed, and effect sizes and odds ratios (ORs) were calculated to quantify between-group differences. Coccidiosis-positive sheep had significantly higher frequencies of diarrhea, dehydration, pale mucous membranes, poor body condition, and reduced appetite (\(p<0.05\)). The mean OPG was \(2846 \pm 1412\), with an approximate \(95\%\) confidence interval of \(2455-3237\) OPG. Coproantigen ELISA demonstrated greater sensitivity (\(94\%\)) than combined microscopy (\(76\%\)). Infected sheep showed significantly lower RBC counts, hemoglobin concentrations, and packed cell volumes, together with leukocytosis, neutrophilia, and eosinophilia. Hematological differences showed very large effect sizes (Cohen's \(d \approx 1.8-2.4\)), while clinical associations were substantial, including dehydration (OR \(\approx 95\)) and pale mucous membranes (OR \(\approx 33\)). Calculated MCH values (9.66 vs. 10.18 pg) and related erythrocyte indices indicate predominantly normocytic, normochromic to mildly hypochromic anemia rather than strictly microcytic normochromic anemia. These findings demonstrate that coccidiosis can produce clinically and hematologically important disease in adult sheep and should be considered in animals presenting with diarrhea, dehydration, reduced appetite, and weight loss. Coproantigen ELISA may provide improved detection of Eimeria infection compared with microscopy alone.

title: Predicting Barriers to Talent Management Implementation in Saudi Universities: A Stochastic Modeling Approach
abstractText: Talent management (TM) has become vital to higher education institutions (HEIs) in Saudi Arabia as they endeavor to attain the goals of Vision 2030. However, there are several barriers to effective implementation of TM that impact on organizations and competitive advantage. The study seeks to predict and estimate the barriers to implementation of the TM practices in Saudi Universities using the stochastic modeling procedure, and provide a new statistical way to analyze the temporal dynamics of TM barriers. This study adopted a cross-sectional, exploratory design with a total of 450 faculty and administrators from different Saudi Universities, with a response rate of 425 faculty and administrators (N=425). A content validated questionnaire tool with 26 items representing the TM barriers was adapted and applied to the five parameters: Identifying Critical Job Positions, Talent Acquisition Practices, Competency Training, Talent Development and Rewards Management. The progression of barriers with time has been assessed using the Modified Weibull Distribution and the predictive models have been developed. The influence of this category on the other categories was shown by the results of the stochastic model, which gave a high value for the ICJP barrier of ($\alpha_{1}=3.421$). The TAP barrier parameter ($\alpha_{2} = 1.783$) was much smaller than the CT barrier parameter ($\beta_{1} = 2.568$) and TD barrier parameters ($\beta_{2}= 2.847$). The lowest influencing parameter found is the RM barrier parameter ($\mu = 1.500$). Systemic barriers must be removed, with a strategy around the allocation of resources, policy adjustment and culture change. By using the stochastic modeling approach, university leaders can have a quantitative forecasting tool ahead of time to proactively manage potential barriers, helping to develop an evidence-based TM strategy.

title: Association of Serum Asprosin, Chemerin, and Omentin-1 Levels with Insulin Resistance and Oxidative Stress in Adults with Obesity: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Obesity disrupts adipokine secretion, insulin sensitivity, and redox homeostasis, yet the integrated relationships among asprosin, chemerin, omentin-1, and oxidative-stress markers have not been comprehensively evaluated in Iraqi adults. This comparative cross-sectional study therefore assessed serum asprosin, chemerin, and omentin-1 in relation to insulin resistance and oxidative stress in 100 adults recruited in Baghdad -- 50 with BMI-defined obesity and 50 normal-weight controls. Anthropometric indices, fasting glucose, insulin, lipid profile, thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS) expressed as malondialdehyde (MDA) equivalents, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), total glutathione, and the three adipokines were measured; HOMA-IR was calculated. Primary group comparisons with effect sizes and 95\% confidence intervals were supplemented by exploratory subgroup, pooled-correlation, regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Adults with obesity exhibited significantly higher BMI, waist circumference, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, MDA-equivalents, asprosin, and chemerin, alongside lower HDL-cholesterol, TAC, total glutathione, and omentin-1 (all \(p < 0.001\)), with large effect sizes for HOMA-IR and all six adipokine-redox biomarkers. In exploratory subgroup analyses within the obesity group, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and MDA-equivalents remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the asprosin difference was nominal. MDA-equivalents and asprosin retained positive coefficients in the age- and sex-adjusted biochemical covariation model. Overall, obesity was characterized by a coordinated pattern of elevated asprosin and chemerin, reduced omentin-1, heightened insulin resistance and TBARS-reactive lipid peroxidation, and diminished antioxidant defence. These cross-sectional, single-center associations are hypothesis-generating rather than diagnostic; they demonstrate internal coherence but do not establish causality, independent adiposity-related effects, or clinical utility. Prospective multicenter studies with balanced obesity subgroups, direct adiposity assessment, within-group and adiposity-adjusted models, and external validation are required before these biomarkers can be considered for clinical risk assessment or screening.

title: Isolation and Functional Characterization of Biosurfactant-Producing Bacteria with Multiple Plant Growth-Promoting Traits from Petroleum-Contaminated Soil
abstractText: Petroleum-contaminated soils harbor diverse microorganisms with unique metabolic traits that can be exploited for sustainable agriculture. The goal of this study was to isolate and characterize bacteria capable of producing biosurfactants and promoting plant growth. Bacterial strains were isolated from petroleum-contaminated soil samples taken from four different sites around Hazira Port in Surat, Gujarat. Eleven bacterial isolates (PS1--PS11) were obtained after enrichment in Mineral Salt Medium (MSM) containing olive oil and screened for biosurfactant production using oil spreading, hemolysis, bacterial adhesion to hydrocarbons, drop-collapse, and emulsification index (E24) assays. Among them, isolate PS5 showed the highest biosurfactant activity, with an 8.9 cm oil displacement zone, $\beta$-hemolysis, 32\% cell surface hydrophobicity, positive drop-collapse activity, and 21.6\% emulsification index. Based on morphological and biochemical characteristics, PS5 was identified as \textit{Pseudomonas aeruginosa}. Furthermore, the selected isolate demonstrated a wide variety of plant growth-promoting characteristics. This included ACC deaminase activity, the synthesis of indole-3-acetic acid, ammonia, and siderophores, as well as the ability to solubilize essential minerals like phosphate, potassium, and zinc. Seed bacterization with \textit{P. aeruginosa} PS5 significantly enhanced seed germination, seedling growth, biomass, and vigor of \textit{Vigna radiata} under laboratory conditions. These findings suggest that \textit{P. aeruginosa} PS5 is a promising multifunctional bacterial candidate for sustainable agricultural applications, warranting further biosafety assessment and field evaluation.

title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
abstractText: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.

title: An Interpretable AutoML-Based Ensemble Framework with Fuzzy Feature Ranking for Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction
abstractText: Cervical cancer is one of the major causes of deaths from cancers among women across the world, which makes it very important to identify women who are at risk early. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have shown potential results in predicting risk of cervical cancer, but many existing methods are dependent on traditional feature selection techniques, manual optimization, and black-box predictive models that lack interpretability. In order to overcome such challenges, this paper introduces an interpretable Fuzzy Rank-H2O AutoML framework that incorporates uncertainty-based feature selection, automated ensemble learning, and XAI. The developed Fuzzy Rank Feature Selection (FRFS) algorithm selects the best set of predictors by evaluating their statistical significance, information gain, clinical importance, and uncertainty. Selected features are then utilized by the H2O AutoML framework to automatically build ensemble models. For improving the model interpretability, SHAP and LIME methods are used to get global feature importance and patient-level explanation as well. The proposed framework was tested on two publicly available cervical cancer datasets independently through stratified five-fold cross-validation, where the SMOTE algorithm is applied to the training datasets in every fold only in order to avoid information leakage. The experimental results on two publicly available datasets show that the proposed framework performs better than the traditional machine learning models and the baseline H2O AutoML framework with the highest accuracy rate of 95.1\% and AUC of 98.1\%. The use of the uncertainty-aware feature selection, automated ensemble learning, and explainability at two levels enables obtaining the accurate, robust, and interpretable predictions.

title: Physical Constraints in Molecular Communication: 2D Diffusion in Stiff and Crowded Hydrogels
abstractText: Diffusion is a fundamental process that governs molecular transport in biological systems and is influenced by the physical and chemical properties of the surrounding environment, including matrix stiffness and molecular crowding. In this study, we developed a two-dimensional hydrogel-based model to investigate how these factors modulate diffusion. Two concentrations of agarose gels (\(1\%\) w/v and \(2\%\) w/v) were taken to represent differences in matrix stiffness, while \(10\%\) w/v sucrose was introduced to create a crowding effect in respective conditions. In our setup, four experimental conditions were designed and analysed, i.e. baseline condition A (\(1\%\) w/v agarose), condition B (\(1\%\) w/v agarose with \(10\%\) w/v sucrose), condition C (\(2\%\) w/v agarose), and condition D (\(2\%\) w/v agarose with \(10\%\) w/v sucrose). Diffusion of methylene blue in four hydrogel conditions was monitored for over 24 hours, and radial spread of dye was quantified by image analysis using ImageJ. The mean squared radius (\(r^2\)) followed a linear relationship with time across all conditions in agreement with Fickian diffusion. However, effective diffusion was progressively reduced from baseline to respective conditions (A \(>\) B \(>\) C \(>\) D), with a percentage reduction of \(6.9\%\) on introducing crowding in condition B, \(14.5\%\) under stiffness alone in condition C and \(21.8\%\) under combined constraints in condition D at a significance level of \(p < 0.05\). These observations and results indicate that stiffness and crowding have an independent and additive effect on restricting molecular transport. This model provides a simple framework for understanding how physical limitations can influence diffusion-driven processes in complex biological environments.

Stability analysis across 100 bootstrap trials yields 89.6\% feature-ranking consistency for SCITFS compared with 67.4\% for mRMR, and a supplementary comparison against a Jensen--Shannon-divergence-based stability metric corroborates this advantage. SCITFS demonstrates robustness to feature noise up to 20\% contamination. These results, together with an ablation study isolating the contribution of each objective term, establish SCITFS as a reliable feature-selection method for bioinformatics, genomics, cybersecurity, finance, and high-dimensional pattern recognition.

title: A System Dynamics-Based Multi-Objective Optimisation Framework for Interstate Reservoir Operations: Evidence from the Parambikulam--Aliyar Project, India
abstractText: Interstate reservoir systems require operating policies that balance water-supply reliability, flood-risk mitigation, hydropower generation, and operational stability under competing stakeholder demands and hydrological uncertainty. Conventional reservoir operation methods often fail to represent the dynamic interactions and trade-offs inherent in multi-reservoir systems. This study presents a System Dynamics (SD)-based multi-objective optimisation framework for interstate reservoir operations, demonstrated using the Parambikulam Aliyar Project (PAP), India. The proposed framework integrates a monthly SD simulation model with the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) to optimise storage-dependent, seasonally varying operating policies. A calibrated lumped-loss formulation is incorporated to represent aggregate operational losses, while four objectives are simultaneously considered: minimisation of water-supply deficits, minimisation of flood-risk exposure, maximisation of a planning-scale hydropower proxy, and minimisation of release variability. Model calibration and validation demonstrated satisfactory agreement between simulated and observed reservoir behaviour, confirming the reliability of the proposed simulation framework. The optimisation generated diverse Pareto-optimal operating policies representing reliability-oriented, flood-averse, and balanced operational strategies, thereby explicitly revealing trade-offs among the competing objectives. The balanced policy achieved an effective compromise between water-supply reliability, flood-risk reduction, hydropower potential, and operational smoothness, providing flexible decision support for different management priorities. The proposed SD-NSGA-II framework offers a transparent, computationally efficient, and operationally interpretable decision-support tool for planning-scale management of complex interstate reservoir systems and can be readily adapted to other multi-reservoir river basins.

title: Serum Adiponectin, Zinc, Magnesium, and Chromium in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: Associations with HOMA-IR and Glycemic Control
abstractText: To our knowledge, this is the first multicenter Iraqi study to evaluate serum adiponectin together with zinc, magnesium, and chromium within a single analytical framework relating these biomarkers to insulin resistance and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). A multicenter comparative cross-sectional study was conducted in Baghdad, Iraq, from June 2025 to March 2026, including 120 adults comprising 80 patients with T2DM and 40 non-diabetic controls. Patients with T2DM were categorized as controlled (HbA1c $<7\%$, $n=34$) or uncontrolled (HbA1c $\geq7\%$, $n=46$). Fasting glucose, HbA1c, insulin, adiponectin, zinc, magnesium, and chromium were measured using standardized procedures. Associations were evaluated using BMI-adjusted and unadjusted comparisons, false-discovery-rate-controlled correlations, simultaneous-entry multiple linear regression, group $\times$ BMI interaction testing, insulin-exclusion sensitivity analysis, a post-hoc extended sensitivity model incorporating hs-CRP, eGFR, and diabetes duration, and exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis. Compared with controls, patients with T2DM demonstrated significantly higher HOMA-IR ($6.47 \pm 2.87$ vs $1.46 \pm 0.45$; $p<0.001$) and significantly lower concentrations of adiponectin ($7.47 \pm 1.87$ vs $11.27 \pm 1.26~\mu\mathrm{g/mL}$; $p<0.001$), zinc, magnesium, and chromium. HOMA-IR was inversely correlated with adiponectin, magnesium, zinc, and chromium and positively correlated with HbA1c. In the primary multivariable model, lower adiponectin ($\beta=-0.390$), magnesium ($\beta=-0.247$), and chromium ($\beta=-0.148$), together with higher HbA1c ($\beta=0.264$), remained independently associated with increased HOMA-IR, with the model explaining 78.2\% of its variance. These associations remained significant after additional adjustment for hs-CRP, eGFR, and diabetes duration. Overall, lower adiponectin and trace-element concentrations were associated with greater insulin resistance and poorer glycemic control in Iraqi adults with T2DM. However, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Prospective studies and external validation are required before biomarker-based cutoff values can be considered for clinical application.

title: An Interpretable AutoML-Based Ensemble Framework with Fuzzy Feature Ranking for Cervical Cancer Risk Prediction
abstractText: Cervical cancer is one of the major causes of deaths from cancers among women across the world, which makes it very important to identify women who are at risk early. Machine Learning (ML) algorithms have shown potential results in predicting risk of cervical cancer, but many existing methods are dependent on traditional feature selection techniques, manual optimization, and black-box predictive models that lack interpretability. In order to overcome such challenges, this paper introduces an interpretable Fuzzy Rank-H2O AutoML framework that incorporates uncertainty-based feature selection, automated ensemble learning, and XAI. The developed Fuzzy Rank Feature Selection (FRFS) algorithm selects the best set of predictors by evaluating their statistical significance, information gain, clinical importance, and uncertainty. Selected features are then utilized by the H2O AutoML framework to automatically build ensemble models. For improving the model interpretability, SHAP and LIME methods are used to get global feature importance and patient-level explanation as well. The proposed framework was tested on two publicly available cervical cancer datasets independently through stratified five-fold cross-validation, where the SMOTE algorithm is applied to the training datasets in every fold only in order to avoid information leakage. The experimental results on two publicly available datasets show that the proposed framework performs better than the traditional machine learning models and the baseline H2O AutoML framework with the highest accuracy rate of 95.1\% and AUC of 98.1\%. The use of the uncertainty-aware feature selection, automated ensemble learning, and explainability at two levels enables obtaining the accurate, robust, and interpretable predictions.

title: Association of Serum Asprosin, Chemerin, and Omentin-1 Levels with Insulin Resistance and Oxidative Stress in Adults with Obesity: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
abstractText: Obesity disrupts adipokine secretion, insulin sensitivity, and redox homeostasis, yet the integrated relationships among asprosin, chemerin, omentin-1, and oxidative-stress markers have not been comprehensively evaluated in Iraqi adults. This comparative cross-sectional study therefore assessed serum asprosin, chemerin, and omentin-1 in relation to insulin resistance and oxidative stress in 100 adults recruited in Baghdad -- 50 with BMI-defined obesity and 50 normal-weight controls. Anthropometric indices, fasting glucose, insulin, lipid profile, thiobarbituric acid-reactive substances (TBARS) expressed as malondialdehyde (MDA) equivalents, total antioxidant capacity (TAC), total glutathione, and the three adipokines were measured; HOMA-IR was calculated. Primary group comparisons with effect sizes and 95\% confidence intervals were supplemented by exploratory subgroup, pooled-correlation, regression, and receiver operating characteristic analyses. Adults with obesity exhibited significantly higher BMI, waist circumference, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, MDA-equivalents, asprosin, and chemerin, alongside lower HDL-cholesterol, TAC, total glutathione, and omentin-1 (all \(p < 0.001\)), with large effect sizes for HOMA-IR and all six adipokine-redox biomarkers. In exploratory subgroup analyses within the obesity group, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, and MDA-equivalents remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the asprosin difference was nominal. MDA-equivalents and asprosin retained positive coefficients in the age- and sex-adjusted biochemical covariation model. Overall, obesity was characterized by a coordinated pattern of elevated asprosin and chemerin, reduced omentin-1, heightened insulin resistance and TBARS-reactive lipid peroxidation, and diminished antioxidant defence. These cross-sectional, single-center associations are hypothesis-generating rather than diagnostic; they demonstrate internal coherence but do not establish causality, independent adiposity-related effects, or clinical utility. Prospective multicenter studies with balanced obesity subgroups, direct adiposity assessment, within-group and adiposity-adjusted models, and external validation are required before these biomarkers can be considered for clinical risk assessment or screening.

title: Gene Therapy Knowledge Among Nursing Students in Chengalpattu: A Mathematical Modeling Study
abstractText: Gene therapy represents a paradigm shift in modern medicine, offering potential cures for previously untreatable genetic disorders. Despite its growing clinical relevance and increasing integration into healthcare systems, knowledge of gene therapy among future healthcare professionals remains inadequately characterized. This study aimed to (1) assess the level of knowledge regarding gene therapy among B.Sc. Nursing students; (2) examine the association between knowledge level and selected demographic variables; (3) identify specific knowledge gaps in gene therapy concepts; and (4) develop a mathematical model to predict knowledge levels based on demographic characteristics. A quantitative, descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 320 B.Sc. Nursing students at Bhaarath College of Nursing, Bharath Institute of Higher Education and Research, Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu, using a non-probability convenience sampling technique. Data were collected using a 30-item semi-structured knowledge questionnaire. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, chi-square tests, binary logistic regression, and Item Response Theory (IRT) analysis, with significance set at $p < 0.05$. Knowledge assessment revealed that 132 participants (41.25\%) demonstrated inadequate knowledge, 100 (31.25\%) had moderate knowledge, and only 88 (27.50\%) showed adequate knowledge (mean score = 15.84 $\pm$ 6.39). IRT analysis revealed that items on CRISPR technology (difficulty: $b = 2.10$) and vector mechanisms (difficulty: $b = 1.76$) were the most challenging. Chi-square analysis indicated significant associations with gender ($\chi^2 = 16.64$, $p < 0.001$, Cram\'er's $V = 0.228$) and year of study ($\chi^2 = 21.70$, $p = 0.001$, Cram\'er's $V = 0.185$). Binary logistic regression identified year of study as the strongest predictor of adequate knowledge (OR = 2.14, 95\% CI: 1.38-3.31, $p < 0.001$). The predictive model achieved 72.8\% classification accuracy. The majority of B.Sc. Nursing students possess inadequate knowledge of gene therapy. Significant associations with gender and year of study suggest that educational interventions tailored to specific demographic groups could effectively address these knowledge gaps. The identified deficits in CRISPR and vector-related knowledge provide targeted areas for curriculum enhancement.
