title: A Hybrid Machine Learning Framework for Phishing Website Detection Using URL and Host-Based Features with Leakage-Resistant Stacking
abstractText: One of the biggest cybersecurity dangers is phishing websites, which trick users into providing confidential information through fake interfaces. Traditional detection solutions, such as black-list and rule-based methods, are no longer effective against emerging attacks. To address the limitations of existing approaches, this study proposes an integrated machine learning system based on URL and host-based characteristics, designed to improve generalization and avoid data leakage. The proposed model uses two branches, each training a separate classifier on a different feature set (URL and host). These branches are combined using a leakage-resistant Out-Of-Fold (OOF) stacking mechanism that derives meta-features from unseen data. In addition, interaction-based meta-features are added to further boost predictive power. The UCI Phishing Websites Dataset, containing 11,055 instances and 17 selected features, was used to evaluate the model. The experimental results validate the proposed hybrid model, which achieves an accuracy of 92.67\% and an ROC-AUC of 0.9788, outperforming the single feature-based models. Cross-validation shows good generalization with low variance. Feature importance analysis shows that the interaction-based meta-features are highly influential in improving classification accuracy. The model achieves a strong balance between performance, computational efficiency, and interpretability compared with contemporary approaches. Its leakage-resistant design enables unbiased evaluation and real-world applicability in cybersecurity. This work contributes to phishing detection research through hybrid ensemble learning with an emphasis on methodological rigor and extensive performance evaluation.

title: FedTrust-GNN: Federated Learning with Blockchain Trust and Graph Neural Networks for Decentralized Modeling
abstractText: Centralized user modeling systems inherently violate privacy regulations, with catastrophic failure points, opaque trust management mechanisms, and vulnerability to complex adversarial strategies such as poisoning attacks, model inversions, and membership inference. Federated learning (FL) approaches address data privacy issues by training models without centralized data storage. However, they suffer from Byzantine failures, lack of transparent reputation-based trust mechanisms, and inability to harness relational information implicit in user interactions. This paper proposes FedTrust-GNN, a secure and relationally aware decentralized user modeling framework that integrates federated learning, permissioned blockchain, and graph neural networks. The framework employs differentially private federated learning with secure multi-party computation (SMPC) to perform gradient aggregation while providing strong privacy guarantees. A permissioned blockchain using the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) consensus protocol maintains an immutable ledger of participant behaviors, model contributions, and reputation scores, eliminating reliance on a trusted central authority. To model participant relationships, a heterogeneous graph attention network (HGAT) infers dynamic trust scores by capturing multihop trust propagation, collusion patterns, and evolving reputation through attention-based message passing. These trust scores guide a trust-weighted robust aggregation (TWRA) mechanism that combines norm clipping with coordinate-wise median aggregation, achieving Byzantine fault tolerance against up to 30\% malicious participants. Experiments on Federated EMNIST, Stack Overflow, and synthetic datasets with 10,000--100,000 participants demonstrate that FedTrust-GNN achieves 94.2\% accuracy (within 1.3\% of centralized models), reduces successful label-flipping attacks by 82\% (34\% to 6.1\%), improves convergence stability by 41\%, and enables blockchain performance of 1,200 transactions per second with 2.3-second finality, demonstrating its practicality for large-scale deployment.

title: REKONSTRUKSI PERAN GURU DALAM IMPLEMENTASI KURIKULUM JARINGAN SEKOLAH ISLAM TERPADU (JSIT) TERHADAP PENGEMBANGAN CRITICAL THINKING DAN PROBLEM SOLVING: STUDI PUSTAKA KUALITATIF
abstractText: Twenty-first-century education demands transformation in teacher pedagogical practices to develop students’ critical thinking, including in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) across Islamic value-based schools. This article synthesizes empirical research on teacher pedagogical practices in PAI learning and examines their contribution to critical thinking development through thematic synthesis. The study employs a qualitative thematic synthesis approach to 18 relevant empirical studies published between 2015 and 2026 and obtained from national and international journal databases. Analysis identified patterns, trends, and variations in pedagogical practices across schools, madrasah, and Integrated Islamic Schools. The synthesis indicates that active, problem- and project-based strategies, including Problem-Based Learning (PBL), Project-Based Learning (PjBL), and Inquiry Learning, are the practices most consistently associated with critical thinking development in PAI and related subjects such as Fiqh. Their effectiveness is strengthened by integrating faith, knowledge, and morals, while learning motivation developed through Islamic value internalization supports students’ engagement and readiness for higher-order thinking. However, implementation varies according to teacher competence, curriculum load, and limitations in holistic assessment. The novelty lies in comprehensively synthesizing teacher pedagogical practices in PAI across diverse Islamic value-based school contexts, where previous studies have remained fragmented and context-specific. The synthesis also provides a cross-context perspective for understanding how pedagogical strategies interact with religious values and classroom conditions in fostering sustained critical thinking among diverse learners. The findings have implications for strengthening PAI curriculum, enhancing teacher competence, and developing Islamic education policies that are more adaptive to twenty-first-century demands.

title: AI Use and Learning Outcomes Among Undergraduate Students: The Mediating Role of Learning Motivation, Locus of Control, and Learning Preferences
abstractText: Background. The growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has created new opportunities for personalized learning, although its contribution to student achievement remains theoretically and empirically contested. Purpose. This study examined the direct and indirect effects of AI use on conceptual understanding and problem-solving ability through learning motivation, locus of control, and learning preferences. Method. A quantitative explanatory design was employed with 88 pre-service teachers enrolled in an Instructional Media course at a teacher education institution in Central Java, Indonesia. Data were collected using validated questionnaires and cognitive assessments. Preliminary analyses were conducted using SPSS, while the measurement and structural models were evaluated through PLS-SEM with 5,000 bootstrap subsamples. Novelty. This study simultaneously tested three psychological and learning-related mediators within a single structural model, thereby extending previous research that primarily examined the direct relationship between AI use and academic performance. Results. AI use significantly predicted learning motivation and locus of control but did not significantly influence learning preferences. Learning motivation significantly predicted learning outcomes and mediated the relationship between AI use and learning outcomes. In contrast, locus of control and learning preferences showed no significant mediating effects. The direct effect of AI use on learning outcomes was also nonsignificant. Conclusion. AI contributes to student learning primarily by strengthening learning motivation rather than through direct technological exposure. Effective AI integration should therefore emphasize reflective, autonomous, and cognitively engaging learning activities.

Financial Literacy, Self-Control, Pay-Later Use, and Financial Management among University of Bengkulu Accounting Students
abstractText: Background: The rapid adoption of buy now, pay later (BNPL) services among university students has intensified concerns about budgeting, debt control, and responsible digital credit use. Objective: This study examines the associations of financial literacy, self-control, and pay-later use with financial management among Accounting students at the University of Bengkulu. Method: A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire. Participants were selected purposively from active Accounting students who had used at least one pay-later platform during the preceding three months. Of the 260 questionnaires distributed, 236 complete responses were obtained; after the prespecified residual screening reported in the source data, 217 responses were analyzed. Multiple linear regression was performed using IBM SPSS Statistics 26. Results: Financial literacy (B = 0.195; β = 0.177; p < 0.001), self-control (B = 0.554; β = 0.575; p < 0.001), and the composite pay-later-use construct (B = 0.152; β = 0.276; p < 0.001) were positively associated with financial management. The model explained 76.5% of the observed variance (R² = 0.765; adjusted R² = 0.762). Conclusion: Among the sampled students, stronger financial literacy and self-control were associated with better financial management. The positive coefficient for pay-later use should be interpreted as reflecting responsible and informed engagement, because the construct also includes risk awareness and usage literacy. The cross-sectional, purposively sampled design does not establish causality or population-wide representativeness.

title: From Point Clouds to IFC-Compliant BIM: A Pipeline for Geometric Modeling of Arch Dam Bodies
abstractText: Abstract Dams are vital infrastructure for water resource management, flood control and hydropower generation, yet their long-term safety is increasingly challenged by aging structures and limited monitoring practices. As-built building information modeling (BIM) provides precise digital representations of existing conditions and supports life cycle management. However, conventional BIM pipelines, largely developed for buildings and standardized infrastructure, are not well-suited to hydraulic structures with highly customized geometries such as arch dams. To address this limitation, an Industry Foundation Class (IFC)-compliant BIM approach for geometric modeling of arch dam bodies using point cloud data is proposed. First, IFC-compliant templates are primarily designed for dam bodies, enabling standardized and expressive digital modeling of dam structures. A reconstruction pipeline is then proposed for geometric modeling of the dam body from unstructured point cloud data, integrating semantic segmentation with parametric geometric modeling techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed pipeline is demonstrated through a case study on a masonry arch dam, where point clouds captured by mobile laser scanning are processed to generate IFC-compliant BIM models. Results indicated that the method enables accurate reconstruction of complex dam geometries while ensuring interoperability within the BIM environment.

title: Knowledge-Guided Temporal Representation Learning for Air Pollution Forecasting (A Case Study of Nasiriyah City)
abstractText: Air pollution prediction is a key research problem due to its direct impact on public health and the urban environment. Moreover, because air pollutants are dynamic and nonlinear, this poses a complex challenge for time-series modeling. However, while there has been significant development in the use of deep learning–based models for air quality prediction, the vast majority of existing methods are primarily data-driven, concentrating solely on reducing prediction errors in the observed value space while neglecting the modeling quality and stability of the learned temporal representations. In this work, we introduce the Knowledge-Guided Temporal Representation Learning (KG-TRL) framework for improving prediction performance. The proposed methods derive from dual-space optimization extended with temporal structure, enhancing prediction accuracy and enabling the mechanism to organize the underlying temporal representations in a dedicated space to maintain the consistency and stability of the extracted temporal components. Experimental on-air pollution data from Nasiriyah, Iraq. The results further validate that the proposed technique exhibits stable learning and significantly better predictions.

title: Hubungan Pengetahuan dan Sikap dengan Kesiapsiagaan dalam Menghadapi Bencana Tsunami pada Petugas Kesehatan Puskesmas di Wilayah VI Jampang Kulon Kabupaten Sukabumi
abstractText: Indonesia sebagai negara yang terletak di kawasan Cincin Api Pasifik sangat rentan terhadap bencana alam, khususnya tsunami. Kesiapsiagaan tenaga kesehatan di puskesmas menjadi elemen kritis dalam mitigasi dampak bencana. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis hubungan antara pengetahuan dan sikap dengan kesiapsiagaan petugas kesehatan Puskesmas di Wilayah VI Jampang Kulon Kabupaten Sukabumi dalam menghadapi bencana tsunami. Metode penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain cross-sectional. Populasi penelitian adalah seluruh petugas kesehatan puskesmas di Wilayah VI Jampang Kulon yang berjumlah 473 orang, dengan sampel sebanyak 216 responden yang dipilih menggunakan teknik stratified random sampling. Instrumen penelitian berupa kuesioner yang telah diuji validitas dan reliabilitasnya. Analisis data meliputi univariat menggunakan distribusi frekuensi dan bivariat menggunakan uji chi-square. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan sebagian besar responden memiliki tingkat pengetahuan cukup (45,4%), sikap positif (57,4%), dan kesiapsiagaan hampir siap (45,4%). Uji chi-square menunjukkan terdapat hubungan yang signifikan antara pengetahuan dengan kesiapsiagaan (p-value = 0,001) dan antara sikap dengan kesiapsiagaan (p-value = 0,001). Disimpulkan terdapat hubungan pengetahuan dan sikap dengan kesiapsiagaan tenaga kesehatan puskesmas di Wilayah VI Jampang Kulon Kabupaten Sukabumi. Rekomendasi diberikan kepada institusi untuk meningkatkan program pelatihan dan sosialisasi kebencanaan secara berkala. Abstract Indonesia, as a country located within the Pacific Ring of Fire, is highly vulnerable to natural disasters, particularly tsunamis. The preparedness of health workers at community health centers is a critical element in mitigating the impact of disasters. This study aims to analyze the relationship between knowledge and attitudes and the preparedness of health workers at community health centers in Region VI Jampang Kulon, Sukabumi Regency, in facing a tsunami disaster. The research method used a quantitative approach with a cross-sectional design. The study population consisted of all health workers at community health centers in Region VI Jampang Kulon, totaling 473 people, with a sample of 216 respondents selected using stratified random sampling. The research instrument was a questionnaire that had been tested for validity and reliability. The research instrument consists of a questionnaire that has been validated and found to be reliable. Data analysis included univariate analysis using frequency distributions and bivariate analysis using the chi-square test. The results of the study indicate that the majority of respondents have a moderate level of knowledge (45.4%), a positive attitude (57.4%), and a state of near-readiness (45.4%). The chi-square test indicated a significant association between knowledge and preparedness (p-value = 0.001) and between attitude and preparedness (p-value = 0.001). It was concluded that there is a relationship between knowledge and attitude and the preparedness of health center staff in Region VI Jampang Kulon, Sukabumi Regency. Recommendations are provided to the institution to improve disaster training and awareness programs on a regular basis

title: Region-based steel fiber placement in reinforced concrete beams under flexure: A critical review and mechanics-informed framework
abstractText: Steel fibers can improve crack control, post-cracking stiffness, ductility, and energy absorption of reinforced concrete beams; however, their efficient placement in critical load-resisting regions remains insufficiently clarified. This critical review synthesizes published evidence and structural-mechanics considerations to develop a mechanics-informed framework for region-based steel fiber placement under four-point bending. The beam is conceptually divided into a constant-moment region and two combined moment–shear regions. The reviewed evidence and mechanics-based interpretation suggest that fibers in the constant-moment region may primarily contribute to flexural crack control and post-cracking stiffness, whereas fibers in the combined moment–shear regions may contribute to restraining inclined cracking and influencing flexural–shear behavior. Fiber location, fiber content, and longitudinal reinforcement are identified as principal comparative variables, while fiber geometry, concrete properties, and testing conditions are treated as contextual factors. The framework further distinguishes equal-local-dosage and equal-total-fiber-mass comparisons to separate the influence of fiber location from total fiber consumption. It provides testable comparison principles for evaluating crack control, post-cracking response, failure behavior, and material efficiency. Experimental validation is required before the relative effectiveness of the proposed placement schemes can be established.

title: Exploring Subjectivity Types of Community Health Visiting Nurses' Core Competencies: A Q-Methodological Approach
abstractText: Purpose: This study aimed to identify subjective types of core competencies among community health visiting nurses.Methods: Q-methodology, which focuses on individual subjectivity, was applied. Thirty-two Q-statements were selected and ranked by 40 community health visiting nurses using a forced 9-point distribution from May 10 to June 30, 2025. The data were analyzed using the Personal Computer - Q methodology Analysis(PC-QUANL) program.Results: Four types were identified: the client-centered relational care type (Type I), collaborative decision-making and resource coordination type (Type II), clinical expertise and judgment type (Type III), and community resource linkage type (Type IV). The four types accounted for 52.9% of the total variance, with explanatory powers of 39.6% (Type I), 5.0% (Type II), 4.9% (Type III), and 3.4% (Type IV). Across the types, trust-based relationships emerged as a recurrent priority, whereas collaboration and resource coordination, clinical expertise and judgment, and community resource linkage differentiated the types.Conclusion: These findings clarify how community health visiting nurses subjectively prioritize core competencies and may be considered when designing competency education and ongoing competency-development strategies for these nurses.

title: The accretion rate resulting in the initial mass function
abstractText: Abstract The aim of this study is to provide a description of the stellar initial mass function (IMF) using the framework of non-extensive statistical mechanics. We seek to demonstrate that the Tsallis distribution, characterized by a single analytical form, can successfully reproduce the full shape of the stellar IMF, from sub-stellar objects to massive stars, without the need for multi-segment or composite models. We adopt the Tsallis distribution derived from non-extensive statistics to model the IMF and perform a detailed comparison with the Kroupa form (Mon Not R Astron Soc 322:231–246, 2001, https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1365-8711.2001.04022.x ). The model parameters, including the non-extensivity index q and the characteristic mass scale $$m_0$$ m 0 , are obtained by fitting the distribution to observational IMF data. Furthermore, we establish a dynamical interpretation of the Tsallis form through an analytical relation between the IMF and linear accretion rates. The Tsallis distribution reproduces the adopted IMF representation with high accuracy using only two parameters. The best-fit values, $$q = 1.40\pm 0.01$$ q = 1.40 ± 0.01 and $$m_0 = 0.086\pm 0.008\,M_\odot$$ m 0 = 0.086 ± 0.008 M ⊙ , yield an asymptotic power-law slope $$\alpha = 2.5$$ α = 2.5 , consistent with the Salpeter and Kroupa exponents. The model naturally reproduces the low-mass turnover near the hydrogen-burning limit and the high-mass power-law tail without requiring discontinuities. The derived analytical relation shows that, within the adopted formulation, the Tsallis form of the IMF corresponds to an accretion-rate dependence of the form $$\dot{m}=a+bm$$ m ˙ = a + b m . The non-extensivity parameter $$q$$ q may therefore provide a phenomenological characterization of fluctuations or correlations in star-forming systems. Establishing a direct connection between $$q$$ q and specific physical properties of the star-forming medium, however, requires further investigation.

title: Factors associated with gait recovery following surgery for degenerative cervical myelopathy
abstractText: OBJECTIVE The objective was to quantify perioperative gait spatiotemporal parameters (STPs) in patients with degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM) and to identify baseline predictors of gait recovery. METHODS This study evaluated a prospective observational cohort at a single academic center. Participants with DCM (n = 59) and non-DCM controls with cervical radiculopathy (n = 13) completed GAITRite walkway assessments at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months after standard-of-care treatments including surgery. STPs included gait speed, step/stride length, cadence, double support time, stride width, and Enhanced Gait Variability Index (eGVI). Relationships between STPs and common clinical scales, including the modified Japanese Orthopaedic Association lower extremity (mJOA-LE) subscore, Nurick grade, and Neck Disability Index (NDI), were evaluated with the Spearman ρ test. The Welch/Wilcoxon tests and linear mixed-effects models were used for between-group and longitudinal comparisons, respectively. Multivariable linear regression modeling was performed to evaluate independent predictors of gait recovery at last follow-up, including age, baseline STPs, mJOA-LE score, and Nurick grade. RESULTS At baseline, subjects with DCM demonstrated a distinct gait phenotype as compared to controls, characterized by significantly reduced gait speed (median [IQR] 83.1 [50.4–101.4] vs 105.1 [91.0–118.1] cm/sec, p = 0.003), shorter step length (51.7 [37.8–60.5] vs 59.1 [56.4–65.4] cm, p = 0.007), and shorter stride length (103.5 [75.1–120.3] vs 118.4 [113.0–130.4] cm, p = 0.006). Subjects with DCM also exhibited greater double support time (36.8% [32.7%–47.1%] vs 34.1% [30.8%–36.1%], p = 0.040) and lower cadence (95.1 [76.7–104.7] vs 103.7 [98.0–114.7] steps/min, p = 0.014). In contrast to NDI, mJOA-LE and Nurick scores showed significant correlations with STPs. After surgery, most STPs improved at 6 months and largely plateaued by 12 months. In multivariable models, the baseline value of each STP was the strongest predictor of change at last follow-up (all p < 0.01), with poorer baseline spatiotemporal performance predictive of greater interval recovery. Older age independently attenuated gains in gait speed and step/stride length (p ≤ 0.04). Baseline mJOA-LE and Nurick scores were not independent predictors of recovery after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS DCM is characterized by a slower and unstable gait with shorter stride lengths that significantly improves by 6 months after surgery and then plateaus. Baseline STPs track disease severity and postoperative gait recovery. Recovery magnitude depends primarily on baseline spatiotemporal performance and is attenuated by age, supporting the use of STPs and age-based stratification for prognostication.

title: A complementary amino acid formulation enhances exercise-induced skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training
abstractText: [Purpose] This study investigated whether a five-amino-acid formulation integrating complementary anabolic, metabolic, and redox-supporting functions enhances skeletal muscle remodeling during resistance training.[Methods] Male C57BL/6N mice were assigned to eight groups receiving vehicle, leucine (300 mg/kg), or amino acid formulation (150-1,500 mg/kg). All mice completed four weeks of ladder resistance training, while the assigned supplements were administered orally once daily. Muscle function, body composition, gastrocnemius fiber cross-sectional area (CSA), anabolic and metabolic signaling proteins, the muscular NAD+/NADH ratio, and circulating markers of muscle damage, inflammation, and glutathione status were assessed.[Results] The formulation improved grip strength at doses of 600-1,500 mg/kg and increased gastrocnemius fiber CSA at 1,200 and 1,500 mg/kg compared with vehicle (p < 0.05), without affecting body weight, food intake, body composition, or absolute muscle mass. It also enhanced AKT-related signaling and increased the expression of PGC-1α, citrate synthase, and UCP3. Several anabolic and mitochondrial protein responses exceeded those observed with leucine alone. The NAD+/NADH ratio increased at doses of 150, 900, and 1,200 mg/kg, with the greatest response observed at 900 mg/kg. The formulation reduced circulating TNF-α at a dose of 1,200 mg/kg, produced a dose-related decrease in CKM that approached statistical significance at 1,500 mg/kg, and most prominently increased total and reduced glutathione levels at 900 mg/kg.[Conclusion] The complementary amino acid formulation enhanced functional, structural, anabolic, metabolic, and redox adaptations during resistance training. These coordinated effects support its potential as a nutritional strategy for improving skeletal muscle quality during chronic resistance exercise.

title: The Role of Job Satisfaction in Mediating the Impact of Work Environment and Compensation on the Performance of BAPPEDA Malang City Employees
abstractText: This study aims to explore the impact of the work environment and compensation on employee performance, emphasizing the mediating role of job satisfaction within a public sector context. Employing a quantitative explanatory design with a saturated sampling technique on all employees at the Regional Development Planning Agency (Bappeda) of Malang City, data were analyzed using the Partial Least Squares (SmartPLS) method. The findings reveal that while the work environment does not directly affect employee performance, it significantly impacts job satisfaction; similarly, compensation significantly affects job satisfaction, which ultimately acts as a vital mediating variable translating both work environment and compensation into enhanced employee performance. Although limited by its scope to a single local government agency, the study provides practical implications emphasizing that public sector management must actively foster job satisfaction to ensure workplace conditions and compensation successfully translate into higher productivity. Ultimately, this research contributes to organizational behavior literature by demonstrating that a favorable work environment alone is insufficient to boost performance unless it effectively drives internal job satisfaction.

title: Adolescents’ perspectives on socio-cultural influences on overweight and obesity in African countries: a systematic scoping review of qualitative studies
abstractText: Abstract Introduction Adolescent obesity is a global public health concern, with increasing prevalence rates in many African countries. Studies have highlighted diverse social and cultural influences on weight, but there is uncertainty about how adolescents in Africa perceive and experience these influences. This review aims to describe adolescents’ perspectives on how cultural beliefs and norms, peers, family, and media influence weight-related behaviours, body weight, and experiences of weight stigma in African countries. Methods We systematically searched Scopus, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CINAHL, PsycINFO and SocINDEX for qualitative studies on socio-cultural determinants of adolescents’ overweight and obesity in African countries. Study quality was assessed using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) for qualitative research. Using a narrative synthesis approach guided by socio-cultural theory, we summarised and interpreted findings across studies to describe adolescents’ perspectives on how cultural beliefs, peers, family, and media influence weight and experiences of weight stigma. Results Of 1,410 articles identified, 17 met the inclusion criteria from eight African countries. Eight studies were conducted in South Africa, while the remaining studies were conducted in Benin, Botswana, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Gambia, Kenya, and Uganda, with no eligible studies identified from Northern or Central Africa. Synthesis of these studies revealed that adolescents perceived peers and parents/families as important influences on their food choices, in the direction of unhealthy options, and on their physical activity levels. Adolescents also described media as shaping these behaviours and perceptions of body image. Several studies reported that overweight or obesity was associated with wealth and health, while thinness was associated with disease or illness. Weight stigma was reported among adolescents irrespective of their weight status. Conclusion Adolescents from eight African countries perceived peers, family members, and media as important socio-cultural influences on their weight-related behaviours, perceptions of body weight, and experiences of weight stigma. Interventions to prevent and manage adolescent obesity may be more effective and better received if these perceived socio-cultural influences are integrated into the design.

title: A High-Density Supercritical Fluid of H2
abstractText: Abstract This study aimed to elucidate the structural evolution of supercritical fluid hydrogen (SCF H2) under high pressure. X-ray diffraction was performed on SCF H2 using synchrotron radiation at room temperature. The structure factor S(Q) was observed in a low-Q region at each pressure, revealing a crossover at around 0.56 GPa, consistent with our previous Raman spectroscopy results. The average volume per molecule was calculated at each pressure using the center-to-center distance between the nearest neighboring H2 molecules, reflecting van der Waals interactions and compression of the internuclear distance. The volumes calculated from the face-centered cubic model were consistent with those derived from the cited equation of state, with a slight discrepancy that increased gradually with the pressure. This finding indicates that further densification following the crossover occurs primarily by intra-atomic/molecular mechanisms rather than intermolecular shortening of distances, which cannot be adequately explained by the close-packed coordination model alone.

THE IMPACT OF FLEXIBLE WORKING HOURS ON EMPLOYEE JOB SATISFACTION
abstractText: To meet individual needs and enhance workplace outcomes, particularly in response to varying employee expectations, flexible working hours are a crucial part of modern working practices. Flexible hours may give workers more control over their time, support work-life balance, and increase job satisfaction. Meanwhile, flexible working arrangements may also create issues for communication, collaboration, and the continuity of working relationships. This study discusses the effect of flexible working hours on staff satisfaction at work, as well as the advantages and obstacles of flexible working arrangements. It also evaluates how flexible working hours affect staff members' desire to stay with their current organizations and their organizational commitment. This study is a quantitative, cross-sectional survey based on Primary data collected using a structured questionnaire. The questionnaire asks about participants' demographic characteristics, such as age, gender, qualifications, work experience, job position, type of organization, and work arrangement. It also includes employees' perceptions of the schedule's effectiveness, work-life balance, job satisfaction, intentions to stay with the organization, working relationships with colleagues, and problems with productivity and communication. Answers to the question highlight employees' perceptions of flexible working hours under remote, hybrid, and on-site work setups. The results emphasize the need for flexible working policies that consider employee autonomy, operational and communication needs, and the team coordination required.

title: Integrative ALS therapy: gene targeted therapy by base editing and potential exercise rehabilitation as synergistic strategies for functional recovery
abstractText: [Purpose] A key pathological hallmark of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is transactive response DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43, encoded by TARDBP) proteinopathy. Mutations in TARDBP and cellular stress can drive nuclear clearance and cytoplasmic aggregation of TDP-43. TDP-43 is an essential nuclear RNA-binding protein that regulates RNA metabolism, and cytoplasmic TDP-43 aggregation leads to aberrant splicing of essential neuronal transcripts including stathmin-2 (STMN2) and unc-13 homolog A (UNC13A). Dysregulated RNA splicing causes cryptic exon (CE) inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A mRNA, resulting in non-functional proteins and disruption of axonal regeneration and synaptic integrity. Splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides and gene-editing platforms can correct STMN2 and UNC13A mis-splicing defects. However, restoring STMN2 and UNC13A expression alone is not sufficient to regenerate neuromuscular junctions or reverse skeletal muscle atrophy, both of which are crucial for functional recovery in patients with ALS.[Methods] We reviewed gene-targeted treatment strategies and rehabilitative mechanisms that inhibit ALS progression and reverse neuromuscular degeneration by analyzing databases, including Google Scholar, PubMed, and ScienceDirect. We proposed a dual-modality therapeutic approach integrating base-editing-mediated gene therapy with exercise-based rehabilitation.[Results] Antisense oligonucleotides and genome editing can restore transcript fidelity by preventing cryptic exons inclusion in STMN2 and UNC13A, thereby stabilizing neuronal function. Gene-targeted therapies halt ALS progression; however, these treatments alone are insufficient to reverse neuromuscular degeneration or achieve functional recovery needed for patients with ALS to return to daily life.[Conclusion] Integrated rehabilitation is a crucial step in gene-targeted therapy for ALS. This strategy halts disease progression and restores neuromuscular function, thereby improving the lifespan and quality of life of patients with ALS.

title: Study of the Association of Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase Activity with Total Bilirubin and Aspartate Aminotransferase in Transfusion-Dependent \(\beta\)-Thalassemia Patients
abstractText: \(\beta\)-Thalassemia is an inherited haemoglobin disorder characterised by ineffective erythropoiesis, chronic haemolysis, repeated transfusion, iron overload, and oxidative stress, all of which can influence liver-related biochemical parameters. The present cross-sectional study was designed to determine the correlation of serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) with total bilirubin and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) in transfusion-dependent \(\beta\)-thalassemia, and to assess whether these associations persisted after adjustment for ferritin, age, and sex. One hundred and fifteen patients with \(\beta\)-thalassemia major were included. Serum GGT and AST activities were assayed by IFCC-traceable enzymatic kinetic methods, total bilirubin by the Jendrassik--Gr\'{o}f diazo method, and ferritin by a chemiluminescent microparticle immunoassay. Relationships were examined using Spearman rank correlations and multivariable linear regression following natural-log transformation of the non-normally distributed variables. The cohort comprised 68 males (59.1\%) and 47 females (40.9\%), with a mean age of \(19.1\pm5.7\) years and a mean transfusion duration of \(16.1\pm5.9\) years. Median GGT, AST, and total bilirubin were 39.2~U/L, 53.3~U/L, and 2.41~mg/dL, respectively. GGT correlated positively with AST (Spearman \(\rho=0.562\), \(p<0.001\)) and, more weakly but significantly, with total bilirubin (\(\rho=0.361\), \(p<0.001\)). Patients with serum ferritin above 2{,}500~ng/mL had significantly higher GGT, AST, and total bilirubin values than those at or below this threshold. In the multivariable log-log model, ln(AST) (\(B=0.656\), \(p<0.001\)) and ln(total bilirubin) (\(B=0.372\), \(p<0.001\)) remained independently associated with ln(GGT), whereas ln(ferritin), age, and sex were not statistically significant after adjustment. The model explained 44.3\% of the variance in ln(GGT) (adjusted \(R^2=0.417\)). These findings indicate that GGT is independently associated with AST and total bilirubin in transfusion-dependent \(\beta\)-thalassemia, supporting their combined interpretation as inexpensive and widely accessible indicators of hepatic and haemolytic stress. Nevertheless, none of these routine biochemical tests can substitute for direct assessment of hepatic iron burden by MRI-based liver iron concentration or for structural evaluation of liver disease by elastography or histopathology. Larger, longitudinal studies incorporating separate bilirubin fractions and dedicated haemolysis markers are warranted to confirm these observations and to clarify their clinical utility in this population.

title: A Hybrid Blockchain and Machine Learning Framework for Loss-Aware Optimization in Distributed Photovoltaic Systems
abstractText: This study proposes a hybrid framework integrating machine learning and blockchain technologies for loss-aware optimization in distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems. The framework combines data-driven loss prediction, decentralized data validation, and optimization-based energy management to improve operational efficiency under variable generation and demand conditions. An LSTM-based model is employed to estimate system losses, while a blockchain layer with smart contracts provides transparent and tamper-resistant execution of operational decisions. The predicted losses are incorporated into the optimization process to determine more efficient energy-routing and grid-interaction strategies. Simulation-based evaluation demonstrates that the proposed framework outperforms the baseline and machine-learning-only configurations. In the investigated case, the energy-loss rate decreases from 14.2% in the baseline scenario to 6.3% with the proposed framework, corresponding to a 55.6% relative reduction. The results also indicate improvements in operational cost and overall system efficiency. These findings demonstrate the potential of combining predictive intelligence with decentralized validation for efficient and secure management of distributed PV systems.

title: Regime-Aware Deployment Validity of Flow-Based IDS
abstractText: Flow-based intrusion detection studies often report strong benchmark scores, but their relevance to future traffic remains uncertain. This paper treats IDS behavior as regime-dependent and proposes an evaluation protocol under temporal shift, family novelty, and combined shift. Flow-only, context-only, selected-context, and full-context XGBoost variants are evaluated on CICIDS2017 and UNSW-NB15 using regime composition, ablations, bootstrap confidence intervals, five-seed sensitivity for corrected family holdouts, diagnostic score distributions, precision–recall analyses, and approximate runtime. CICIDS2017 random-split performance is near perfect, whereas future and family-novel regimes differ sharply. Selected graph-derived context improves Thursday web OOD and combined shift, while full context can reduce transfer. Friday botnet distribution shift and the botnet-family holdout remain severe failures, with zero F1 and recall for several feature sets. In contrast, the record-disjoint UNSW-NB15 Generic/Exploits holdout remains strong for the flow-only model, showing that OOD difficulty is regime-dependent. The results demonstrate that high random-split performance does not establish deployment readiness; temporal evaluation can also mislead when attack-family structure is not separated, and graph-context transfer varies by feature set and operating regime.

title: Selective Adsorption of Methyl Acetate from Model Fischer–Tropsch Synthetic Oil on 13X Zeolite: Experimental and Computational Insights
abstractText: Abstract The efficient removal of ester oxygenates from Fischer–Tropsch (FT) synthetic oil remains challenging due to limited understanding of selective adsorption mechanisms and adsorption kinetics. Herein, a combined experimental and theoretical approach was employed to investigate the selective adsorption behavior, kinetics, and mechanism of removing methyl acetate, a representative ester oxygenate, from a methyl acetate/1-decene/decane model FT synthetic oil using 13X zeolite, γ-alumina, and activated carbon. Dynamic breakthrough experiments revealed that 13X zeolite exhibited substantially higher adsorption selectivity and removal efficiency toward methyl acetate than γ-alumina and activated carbon. The adsorption behavior on 13X zeolite was well described by both pseudo-first-order and pseudo-second-order kinetic models. Moreover, 13X zeolite demonstrated excellent regeneration capability and adsorption stability, maintaining its performance over six consecutive adsorption–desorption cycles. Structural and acidity characterizations indicated that the superior adsorption performance of 13X zeolite originates from its well-developed hierarchical pore structure and abundant Lewis acid sites. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations suggested that the polar carbonyl and ester groups in methyl acetate induce pronounced charge separation on the molecular surface, creating strong positive and negative electrostatic potential regions. These features enable methyl acetate to preferentially adsorb on 13X zeolite through electrostatic (ion–dipole) attraction, hydrogen bonding, and van der Waals forces, effectively displacing weakly polar hydrocarbon molecules from adsorption sites. Monte Carlo (MC) simulations reproduced the experimental adsorption behavior and provided a reliable predictive model for equilibrium adsorption capacity. This work establishes an integrated experimental–computational paradigm for elucidating adsorption mechanisms and predicting oxygenate removal performance, providing a general strategy for the purification of Fischer–Tropsch synthetic oil.

title: Hubungan Pengetahuan Dengan Kepatuhan Minum Obat Pada Penderita Hipertensi Di Kelurahan Baros Wilayah Kerja UPTD Puskesmas Baros Kota Sukabumi
abstractText: Hipertensi merupakan salah satu penyakit tidak menular dengan prevalensi yang terus meningkat dan sering kali tidak terdeteksi secara dini, sehingga kepatuhan dalam mengonsumsi obat menjadi faktor penting dalam pengendalian penyakit. Kepatuhan tersebut dipengaruhi oleh berbagai faktor, di antaranya pengetahuan penderita dan dukungan keluarga. Penelitian ini menggunakan korelasional dengan pendekatan cross sectional. Populasi adalah 1201 penderita hipertensi di Kelurahan Baros Wilayah Kerja UPTD Puskesmas Baros Kota Sukabumi dengan sampel 302 responden yang dipilih menggunakan cluster sampling. Data dikumpulkan menggunakan kuesioner dan dianalisis dengan uji Chi-Square. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan sebagian besar responden memiliki pengetahuan tinggi, dukungan keluarga baik, dan patuh minum obat. Terdapat hubungan pengetahuan (p-value = 0,000; r = 0,251) dan dukungan keluarga (p-value = 0,000; r = 0,400) dengan kepatuhan minum obat pada penderita hipertensi. Terdapat hubungan yang signifikan pengetahuan dan dukungan keluarga dengan kepatuhan minum obat pada penderita hipertensi. Edukasi hipertensi dan dukungan keluarga perlu ditingkatkan untuk meningkatkan kepatuhan minum obat. Abstract Hypertension is a noncommunicable disease with a steadily rising prevalence that often goes undetected in its early stages; consequently, medication adherence is a critical factor in managing the condition. This adherence is influenced by various factors, including the patient’s knowledge and family support. This study aims to examine the relationship between knowledge and family support and medication adherence among patients with hypertension. This study employed a correlational design with a cross-sectional approach. The population consisted of 1201 hypertensive patients in Baros Urban Village (within the service area of ​​the Baros Community Health Center, Sukabumi City), with a sample of 302 respondents selected via cluster sampling. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using the Chi-Square test. The results showed that the majority of respondents possessed a high level of knowledge, received good family support, and were adherent to medication. Significant associations were found between knowledge (p-value = 0.000; r = 0.251) and family support (p-value = 0.000; r = 0.400) with medication adherence among hypertensive patients. There is a significant relationship between knowledge and family support and medication adherence in patients with hypertension. Hypertension education and family support need to be improved to increase medication adherence

title: Generative AI-Assisted Competitive Microlearning Strategy: Development and Validation of the Plomp Model in Classroom Teacher Education in Finland
abstractText: Background. The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education has created challenges in designing responsible and adaptive learning strategies. Meanwhile, competitive elements in gamified learning remain debated due to inconsistent effects on learner engagement. Purpose. This research aimed to develop and evaluate a generative AI-assisted competitive microlearning strategy for improving instructional media development skills among Finnish Luokanopettajakoulutus (Class Teacher Education) students. Novelty. This study introduces a novel instructional design that integrates generative AI, microlearning, and optional quality-based competition. Unlike conventional competitive gamification approaches, the proposed strategy recognizes learner differences by examining whether competition produces varied outcomes across learning groups Method. Using the Plomp development model, the study involved 79 undergraduate students from four parallel classes. Data from expert validation, practicality questionnaires, and product assessments were analyzed using Aiken’s V and descriptive statistics. Results. The strategy achieved high validity (Aiken’s V = 0.87) and strong practicality (83.1% student response; 85.9% lecturer response). Variation in competition participation (41–62%) indicated different effects among learner groups. Conclusion. The findings contribute an adaptive AI-assisted microlearning framework that balances innovation, learner diversity, and educational equity in teacher education.

title: Cortical development in patients with metopic craniosynostosis
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Patients with metopic synostosis have an increased risk of neurodevelopmental disorders, despite a minimal risk of intracranial hypertension. While mechanical constraint due to premature suture fusion has been proposed as a contributing factor, evidence suggests intrinsic brain malformations may play a more significant role. Cortical thickness, volume, and surface area alterations have been implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders, yet their role in metopic synostosis remains unclear. In this retrospective study, authors investigated whether these cortical parameters are altered in patients with metopic synostosis compared with those in healthy controls. METHODS 3D T1-weighted MRI brain scans from patients 0–2 years of age with metopic synostosis were reviewed. Children born preterm or with a syndromic condition were excluded. MRI brain scans of patients and age-matched controls were processed using the Infant FreeSurfer pipeline to quantify cortical thickness, cortical volume, cortical surface area, and intracranial volume. Linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, and intracranial volume were used to compare global cortical thickness, cortical volume, and cortical surface area between the groups, with secondary analyses of these metrics at the lobular level. RESULTS Sixty-four patients with metopic synostosis and 32 controls (median age at MRI 8.4 months [IQR 4.84] and 12.4 months [IQR 9.68], respectively) were eligible for inclusion. Patients with metopic synostosis had a significantly increased cortical surface area compared to that in controls (p = 0.029). No significant differences were found in global cortical thickness (p = 0.281) or total cortical volume (p = 0.141) between patients and controls. CONCLUSIONS Increased cortical surface area is observed in patients with metopic synostosis; however, there are no significant differences in cortical thickness and volume. Similar developmental trajectories have been observed in infants with neurodevelopmental disorders. These findings shift the focus from mechanical deformation to fundamental brain development pathways in patients with metopic synostosis.

title: CAR signaling instructs divergent metabolic reprogramming and functional fates in αβ and γδ T cells
abstractText: Abstract γδ T-cell-based immunotherapies have become relevant as alternatives to conventional αβ T-cell products, with preclinical data demonstrating tumor burden reduction and the mitigation of tumor-induced tissue damage. Given that most CAR constructs have been optimized for αβ T cells, we hypothesized that distinct T-cell types may require tailored CAR architectures to achieve optimal function. To test this hypothesis, we conducted a systematic comparative analysis of γδ and αβ T cells transduced with a second-generation PSCA-targeting CAR (PSCA-8t28z). We found that although γδ and αβ CAR-T cells exhibit comparable levels of cytotoxicity, they differ phenotypically. Through a system-level phosphoproteomic analysis, we identified 307 phosphosites whose abundance differed between γδ and αβ CAR-T cells. Pathway enrichment analysis placed glycolysis/gluconeogenesis and TCR signaling within the top significantly overrepresented signaling networks. The results of functional validation studies confirmed that γδ CAR-T cells have lower glycolytic and oxidative phosphorylation capacity than αβ-CAR-T cells do and weaker activation of activator protein 1 (AP-1). Notably, we identified thioredoxin-interacting protein (TXNIP) as a potential actionable target to enhance γδ CAR-T-cell metabolism. Finally, we designed a new synthetic costimulatory receptor that potentiates AP-1 activation, resulting in improved in vivo persistence. These results highlight the fundamental biological differences between γδ and αβ T cells and support the development of cell type-specific receptor engineering strategies to maximize γδ CAR-T-cell function and therapeutic benefit.

title: Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of Aldimines with Unactivated Alkyl Iodides
abstractText: Abstract A nickel-catalyzed reductive alkylation of directing-group-free N-sulfonyl and N-aryl aldimines is reported. The reaction proceeds at ambient temperature and accommodates unactivated primary, secondary, and tertiary alkyl iodides as well as selected activated alkyl bromides with broad functional-group tolerance. Complex molecule-derived alkyl iodides, a gram-scale reaction, and β-amino ester derivatizations demonstrate synthetic utility. Mechanistic studies support nickel-mediated generation of a solution-accessible alkyl radical and are consistent with outer-sphere radical addition to the imine.

title: Brain tumor surgery outcomes in rural America: a cross-sectional statewide study
abstractText: OBJECTIVE The aim of this study was to evaluate demographic characteristics and predictors of adverse outcomes among rural New York State (NYS) residents undergoing neurosurgical treatment for brain tumor (BT), with the goal of identifying factors contributing to increased healthcare costs and diminished quality of care. METHODS This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed 2010–2020 discharge data from the New York Statewide Planning and Research Cooperative System (SPARCS). Adults (≥ 18 years) who underwent neurosurgical treatment for BT in NYS hospitals were included, excluding patients residing in New York City. Rural residence was defined by US Department of Justice criteria. Sociodemographic variables included age, race/ethnicity, income quartile, and insurance status. Primary outcomes were postoperative length of stay (LOS), location of discharge (home vs nonhome), emergency department (ED) presentation, and 30-day mortality. Univariate and multivariate mixed-effects regression models identified independent predictors of adverse outcomes. RESULTS Among 25,887 patients, 3745 (14%) resided in rural areas. Despite a significant decline in the NYS rural population during the study period (p < 0.001), rural BT neurosurgical admissions increased (p = 0.005). Rural patients were more often White (91% vs 80%, p = 0.0425) and from lower income quartiles (66% vs 39%, p = 0.0015) than nonrural patients. On multivariable analysis, age > 65 years, male gender, and non-White race predicted ED presentation, whereas private insurance was protective. Nonhome discharge and ED presentation were the strongest predictors of prolonged LOS. ED presentation and older age predicted a nonhome discharge, while private insurance favored home discharge. Thirty-day mortality was independently associated with nonhome discharge, male gender, lower income, and longer LOS. Rural residence was not independently associated with any outcome after adjustment. CONCLUSIONS Rural NYS residents undergoing neurosurgical treatment for BT face increasing procedural demand despite a shrinking rural population. Targeted care coordination, improved access pathways, and telemedicine/artificial intelligence–supported interventions may reduce disparities, costs, and adverse outcomes.

title: Evaluation of Leucine in Hydrate-based CO2 Separation Technology for Synthesized Mixture Gas
abstractText: Abstract To increase the combustion calorific value, reduce the greenhouse effect of CO2, and prevent corrosion to pipelines, impurity gases such as CO2 and N2 in biogas must be effectively removed. This study investigates the effects of leucine (Leu) on the kinetics and gas separation efficiency of synthesized ternary (CH4/CO2/N2) gas hydrate formation. The experimental work involved monitoring pressure drop, gas consumption, CH4 recovery, CO2 capture, and separation factor under various conditions of pressure, temperature, and Leu concentration. Advanced characterization techniques, including powder X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, and Cryo-SEM, were employed to analyze hydrate structure, cage occupancy, and crystal morphology. The key findings indicate that 0.5 wt % Leu optimally promotes formation kinetics and enhances gas separation at medium pressures and high supercooling. A trade-off relationship between CH4 recovery and CO2 capture was observed, influenced by Leu concentration and the degree of supercooling. Structural analysis confirmed the formation of sI hydrate with co-occupancy of gas molecules, while morphological studies showed that increased Leu concentration leads to a denser, more uniform crystal arrangement. The promotion mechanism is attributed to the adsorption of Leu’s hydrophobic groups at the hydrate interface, which enhances gas–liquid mass transfer and facilitates nucleation and growth, thereby improving overall kinetic performance and separation effectiveness.

title: Computer Vision System and Transformer-Based Multimodal Fusion of Medical Images for Enhanced Diagnostic Decision Making
abstractText: The rise of artificial intelligence technologies and their increasing reliance in numerous fields, most notably medicine, is significant. AI plays a crucial role in assisting physicians with accurate patient diagnosis, enabling them to make informed decisions. This article presents a method for integrating computer vision technologies into the medical field, where multimodal medical imaging integrates structural and textual information to support clinical decision-making. However, most image fusion frameworks based on transformers remain narrowly designed for a single media combination and a single subsequent task. This paper proposes the Multimodal Adaptive Fusion Transformer (CMAFT), a unified architecture that combines Swin transformer encoders for each media with a Catalyst Cross Attention Fusion Module (GCAF) to dynamically weight each media's contribution based on its real-time reliability. CMAFT was evaluated against two structurally different multimodal reference standards: the BraTS 2021 dataset, in which four MRI sequences (T1, T1ce, T2, FLAIR) were combined to segment brain tumor volumes, and the MIMIC-CXR dataset, in which chest X-ray images were combined with duplex radiology report inclusions to classify multimodal pathology and generate reports. The proposed GCAF module provides a learnable reliability gateway that curbs degraded or lost data streams, while a multiscale hierarchical integration pyramid preserves both fine detail and overall semantic context. Experiments show that CMAFT achieves average Dice scores of 92.4%, 87.9%, and 84.6% for whole tumor, tumor nucleus, and enhanced tumor, respectively, on the BraTS 2021 dataset, and a multi-class average area under the curve (AUC) of 0.876 with an overall F1 value of 0.658 on the MIMIC-CXR dataset, outperforming modern hybrid CNN-Transformer models while using fewer parameters compared to similar dual-code baseline models. Resection studies confirm that both reliability gate and multi-scale integration contribute to measurable gains, and that CMAFT degrades smoothly when either an MRI sequence or radiology report is unavailable. These results suggest that a single adaptive mutual attention integration design can be generalized across volumetric and text-based multimodal diagnostic pathways.

abstractText: Penelitian ini dilatarbelakangi oleh cakupan ASI eksklusif di Desa Panenjoan yaitu di RW 10 sebesar 33,33% dan RW 11 sebesar 35,29%. Tujuan penelitian untuk mengetahui gambaran pengetahuan ibu bayi usia 0-6 bulan tentang ASI eksklusif di Desa Panenjoan Kecamatan Cicalengka Kabupaten Bandung. Pengetahuan merupakan efek lanjutan dari keingintahuan individu. ASI eksklusif adalah memberikan hanya ASI saja tanpa memberikan makanan dan minuman lain kepada bayi usia 0-6 bulan. Jenis penelitian deskriptif dengan populasi 32 responden menggunakan teknik total sampling. Instrumen yang digunakan kuesioner dengan r hitung 0,445-0,660 dan cronbah alpha 0,866. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa gambaran pengetahuan ibu bayi usia 0-6 bulan tentang ASI eksklusif termasuk kategori kurang 62,50%, kategori cukup 25%, dan kategori baik 12,50%. Kesimpulan dari hasil penelitian mayoritas termasuk kategori kurang. Disarankan kepada kader agar bekerja sama dengan puskesmas dalam memberikan edukasi tentang ASI eksklusif. Abstract This research was motivated by the exclusive breastfeeding coverage in Panenjoan Village, namely in RW 10 at 33.33% and RW 11 at 35.29%. The aim of the research was to determine the knowledge of mothers of babies aged 0-6 months about exclusive breastfeeding in Panenjoan Village, Cicalengka District, Bandung Regency. Knowledge is a continuation effect of individual curiosity. Exclusive breastfeeding is giving only breast milk without giving other food and drinks to babies aged 0-6 months. This type of research is descriptive with a population of 32 respondents using total sampling techniques. The instrument used was a questionnaire with an r count of 0.445-0.660 and a cronbah alpha of 0.866. The results of the study showed that the knowledge of mothers of babies aged 0-6 months about exclusive breastfeeding was in the poor category at 62.50%, in the sufficient category at 25%, and in the good category at 12.50%. The conclusions from the majority of research results are in the poor category. It is recommended that cadres collaborate with community health centers in providing education about exclusive breastfeeding.

title: Textile Industry Impact of Wastewater on Soil Health and Nutrient Availability in Semi-Arid Regions: Evidence from Sanganer, Jaipur
abstractText: This study investigated the impact of textile industry wastewater on soil health in Sanganer, Rajasthan (26.81--26.82°N, 75.72--75.77°E), a major textile printing and dyeing hub. Surface soil samples (n = 25, depth 0--30 cm) from five agricultural sites were analyzed for physicochemical properties (pH, EC, OC, CEC, CaCO$_3$), macronutrients (N, P, K, S, Ca, Mg, Na), and micronutrients (Fe, Mn, Zn, Cu, B). Results revealed alkaline soils (pH 8.2--10.6), high electrical conductivity (EC: 0.3--4.8 dS/m), and low organic matter (OM: 0.04--0.32\%). Macronutrient levels were medium to high (N: 147--301 kg/ha; P: 13--36 kg/ha; K: 174--334 kg/ha), while micronutrients showed deficiencies for Zn (0.29--0.52 ppm) and Fe (3.76--4.80 ppm). Strong positive correlations among metallic micronutrients (r > 0.95) indicate common soil factors influencing their availability. Principal component analysis extracted three components explaining 74.5\% of total variance, with PC1 (38.8\%) representing metallic micronutrients and PC2 (19.0\%) representing salinity and CEC. The study underscores the need for periodic soil testing and site-specific nutrient management to enhance sustainable crop productivity in textile-impacted semi-arid regions.

title: Childhood Environmental Unpredictability and Bedtime Procrastination Among Undergraduate Medical Students in South India: A Cross-sectional Study
abstractText: Objective: To examine the association between retrospectively reported childhood environmental unpredictability and bedtime procrastination among undergraduate medical students in South India.Methods: This single-center cross-sectional online survey included 200 undergraduate medical students. Bedtime procrastination was assessed using the nine-item Bedtime Procrastination Scale (BPS; range, 9–45), and childhood unpredictability using the 38-item Questionnaire of Unpredictability in Childhood (QUIC; range, 0–38). Because the BPS has no validated diagnostic cutoff, scores were analyzed continuously. The primary analysis used Spearman rank correlation with bootstrap confidence intervals (CI), and robust linear regression was used to quantify the association. An additional multivariable model adjusted for age, sex, academic year, residence, and socioeconomic category.Results: The mean age was 18.8 years (standard deviation [SD], 1.1), and 67.0% of participants were women. Mean BPS and QUIC scores were 27.93 (SD, 7.19) and 9.39 (SD, 5.53), respectively. Overall QUIC score was weakly associated with BPS score (Spearman rho=0.242; 95% bootstrap confidence interval, 0.111–0.366; p<0.001). After adjustment for age, sex, academic year, residence, and socioeconomic category, a five-point higher QUIC score was associated with a 1.48-point higher mean BPS score (95% CI, 0.52–2.43; p=0.003). Three parental domains showed small exploratory associations after false-discovery-rate adjustment.Conclusion: Childhood environmental unpredictability showed a small positive association with bedtime procrastination. The cross-sectional, retrospective findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish causality.

title: The Impact of Adverse Childhood Experiences on Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among Korean Adolescents: Moderating Effects of Social Support and Risk Profiling of Vulnerable Subgroups
abstractText: Purpose: This study examined the prevalence of non-suicidal self-injury(NSSI) among Korean adolescents and investigated the independent and interactive associations of adverse childhood experiences(ACEs) and social support with NSSI. Methods: Data from a descriptive cross-sectional survey of Korean adolescents were analyzed. Group differences based on NSSI status were evaluated using χ²-test or independent t-test. Hierarchical multiple logistic regression analysis was performed to determine the independent effects of ACEs and social support on NSSI, and to test whether social support moderated the relationship between ACEs and NSSI. Results: Over one-third of the participants reported a past-year history of NSSI. Cumulative ACEs were independently associated with higher odds of NSSI, whereas higher social support was independently associated with lower odds of NSSI, confirming its robust protective role. However, the interaction between ACEs and social support was not statistically significant, indicating that social support exerts a generalized protective effect rather than selectively moderating the association between ACE exposure and NSSI.Conclusion: These findings underscore the need for systemic, early mental health screening within school and community settings that comprehensively assesses ACEs, depressive symptoms, and self-injury risk. Furthermore, prevention strategies should prioritize multi-source support networks involving peers, educators, and professional counselors, alongside evidence-based interventions tailored to enhance emotion regulation and resilience.

title: Effect of Smoking on Serum Prolidase Levels and Selected Biochemical Variables Among Athletes in Kirkuk City
abstractText: Cigarette smoke delivers thousands of chemical constituents to the airway and systemic circulation, many of which are directly oxidising or pro-inflammatory. Because habitual physical training itself perturbs oxidative and mineral homeostasis, athletes who smoke sit at the intersection of two opposing physiological pressures, making them a biologically informative --- yet under-studied --- population in which to examine smoking-related biochemical change. This cross-sectional study compared serum prolidase, iron, ferritin, zinc, calcium, magnesium, selenium and reduced glutathione (GSH) in 60 smoker and 40 non-smoker male athletes (18--30 years) recruited from sports clubs in Kirkuk City, Iraq. Smoker athletes showed significantly lower serum prolidase, selenium, calcium and GSH, and significantly higher iron and ferritin, than non-smoker athletes; zinc and magnesium did not differ. None of the seven correlations between prolidase and the remaining biochemical variables reached significance among smokers ($n = 60$). To address multiplicity and effect magnitude, standardized mean differences (Hedges' $g$), 95\% confidence intervals, and Holm--Bonferroni-adjusted significance were calculated for all eight comparisons. After adjustment, the iron, ferritin, selenium and GSH differences remained significant, whereas the prolidase and calcium differences no longer met the corrected threshold. These findings indicate that smoking is associated with a shift in oxidative and trace-element balance in athletes and should be interpreted as an association rather than proof of a causal effect.

title: Factors Associated with Health-Promoting Behaviors among Late Middle-Aged Women: Focusing on Aging Anxiety, Social Support, Self-Efficacy, and Physiological Indicators
abstractText: Purpose: The purpose of this study was to identify the relationships between aging anxiety, social support, and self-efficacy, and to determine the factors influencing health-promoting behaviors among late middle-aged women. Methods: This study utilized a descriptive research design. The participants were 136 late middle-aged women visiting vocational training centers in Sejong Special Self-Governing City. Data were collected using structured questionnaires regarding general characteristics, aging anxiety, social support, and self-efficacy. Physiological indicators, including blood glucose levels and body mass index (BMI), were also measured. Results: The factors significantly influencing health-promoting behaviors in late middle-aged women were social support (β=.40, p<.001), subjective health status categorized as "healthy" (β=.27, p=.019) or "average" (β=.29, p=.009), blood glucose levels (β=.17, p=.010), BMI (β=.16, p=.012), and aging anxiety (β=-.16, p=.042). These factors explained 48.9% of the total variance in health-promoting behaviors (adjusted R²=.489). Conclusion: The findings suggest that psychological, social, and physiological factors should be considered when developing health promotion strategies for late middle-aged women. Community-based programs that enhance social support and nursing interventions addressing health perception, aging anxiety, and physiological health management may help support health-promoting behaviors in this population.

Flue Gas Torrefaction of Corn Stover-Densified Fuel: Impacts on Physicochemical Properties and Combustion Performance
abstractText: Abstract Corn stover pellets were torrefied under a simulated flue gas atmosphere (220 °C–300 °C, 15–25 min) to evaluate physicochemical and combustion modifications. Analyses revealed that increasing torrefaction severity significantly reduced the volatile matter, hydrogen, and oxygen contents, while enriching the fixed carbon and ash fractions. Consequently, the higher heating value increased by up to 33.41%, peaking at an energy density of 1.33, albeit at the expense of a sharp decline in mass yield. Thermogravimetric analysis revealed that increasing torrefaction severity elevated the ignition temperatures while reducing burnout temperatures. Mild torrefaction (220–240 °C, 15–20 min) maintained optimal combustion stability; conversely, severe conditions (>260 °C, >20 min) significantly deteriorated the combustion kinetics, as evidenced by a marked reduction in both the maximum combustion rate and the comprehensive combustion characteristic index.

title: Ocular Tuberculosis in Advanced Proliferative Diabetic Retinopathy: A Diagnostic and Therapeutic Dilemma in A Vitrectomized Eye
abstractText: Background: Ocular tuberculosis (OTB) is a paucibacillary extrapulmonary infection, hard to recognize in an eye compromised by proliferative diabetic retinopathy (PDR) and vitreoretinal surgery, where postoperative inflammation, tamponade artifacts, hemorrhage and diabetic microangiopathy mimic infectious uveitis. Objective: To characterize the diagnosis, molecular confirmation, and longitudinal outcomes of occult ocular tuberculosis in a vitrectomized eye with end-stage proliferative diabetic retinopathy. Methods: A 50-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and pulmonary tuberculosis presented with acute inflammation (OD) 5 days after pars plana vitrectomy. He was followed over six milestones (T0–T5, 16 weeks) with SD-OCT and vitreous nested RT-PCR (IS6110/MPB64); outcomes were best-corrected acuity (LogMAR), intraocular pressure and central macular thickness (CMT). Results: At T0 (OD 1/300, LogMAR 2.48) with ciliary flush and gas endotamponade, vitreous RT-PCR was positive for M. tuberculosis DNA (IS6110/MPB64), establishing intraocular tuberculosis masked by surgical inflammation. Quadruple antituberculous therapy (RHZE) with corticosteroids improved vision to 6/30 (LogMAR 0.70) by week 3 and 6/21 (LogMAR 0.54) by week 6. At week 7, SD-OCT unmasked diabetic cystoid macular edema (CMT 365 µm) that responded to sub-Tenon triamcinolone (CMT 340 µm), with final acuity 6/9.5 corrected (LogMAR 0.20) at week 16. The contralateral eye (OS) developed neovascular glaucoma (IOP 51.0–63.0 mmHg) and no light perception, requiring silicone oil evacuation. Conclusion: Ocular tuberculosis must be suspected in atypical intraocular inflammation in vitrectomized eyes, especially with tuberculosis or diabetes. Vitreous PCR is decisive when signs overlap with surgical trauma and diabetic microangiopathy, and prompt antituberculous plus corticosteroid therapy can achieve visual salvage.

abstractText: Penelitian dilatarbelakangi adanya remaja yang merasa tidak puas dengan penampilan fisiknya menyebabkan munculnya perasaan tidak senang, sering merasa cemas akan perubahan yang terjadi pada tubuh mereka misalnya berat badan. Tujuan penelitian untuk mengidentifikasi citra tubuh (body image) pada remaja kelas X di SMA 1 Cisarua Kabupaten Bandung Barat. Citra tubuh (body image) yaitu cara sudut pandang seseorang tentang penampilan pada karakteristik tubuh yang dimilikinya. Remaja adalah masa peralihan dari masa kanak-kanak menuju masa dewasa Desain penelitian deskriptif kuantitatif, populasi sebanyak 207 remaja menggunakan teknik Proportionate Random Sampling. Kuesioner menggunakan The Multidimensional Body Self Relations Questionnaire Appearance Scale (MBSRQ-AS). Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar responden memiliki citra tubuh (body image) positif 68%, sub-variabel tentang evaluasi penampilan kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif 68%, tentang orientasi penampilan kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif 65%, tentang kepuasan terhadap bentuk tubuh kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif (62%), tentang kecemasan menjadi gemuk kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif 100%, dan tentang pengkategorian ukuran tubuh kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif 70%. Kesimpulan penelitian menunjukan kategori citra tubuh (body image) positif dengan hasil 70%. Bagi SMA Negeri 1 Cisarua Kabupaten Bandung Barat dapat mempertahankan citra tubuh (body image) positif dengan melakukan edukasi terkait peningkatan rasa Percaya Diri secara terprogram dan berkelanjutan. Abstract The emergence of feelings of displeasure such as frequent anxiety regarding bodily changes (e.g., weight gain) stemming from dissatisfaction with their physical appearance serves as the background of this study. The study aimed to assess the body image of 10th-grade students at SMA Negeri 1 Cisarua, West Bandung Regency. Body image is defined as an individual's perspective regarding their own physical characteristics and appearance. The period between childhood and adulthood is known as adolescence. A quantitative descriptive research design was employed, utilizing a population of 207 adolescents selected through proportionate random sampling. The Multidimensional Body Self-Relations Questionnaire-Appearance Scale (MBSRQ-AS) was used to construct the study's questionnaire. The results indicate that the majority of respondents (68%) possess a positive body image. Specifically, positive body image ratings were observed in the following areas: appearance evaluation (68%), appearance orientation (65%), body shape satisfaction (62%), anxiety about becoming fat (100%), and body size categorization (70%). Overall, the study concludes that 70% of the respondents exhibit a positive body image. SMA Negeri 1 Cisarua, West Bandung Regency, is encouraged to maintain this positive body image by implementing programmed and sustainable educational initiatives aimed at boosting self-confidence.

title: Hybrid Threat Detection Using Wazuh, DBSCAN, Random Forest, and MISP Threat Intelligence
abstractText: Background: Cyberattacks continue to grow in volume and sophistication, and small-to-medium-sized organizations are increasingly exposed because of limited budgets and security personnel. Open-source Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) platforms such as Wazuh offer a low-cost alternative to commercial solutions; however, their reliance on static, rule-based correlation logic limits their ability to detect previously unseen or evolving threats and tends to generate a high rate of false positives. Objective: This study proposes a layered hybrid detection architecture that combines Wazuh with an unsupervised anomaly-detection stage using Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN), a supervised classification stage using Random Forest, and an enrichment stage using the Malware Information Sharing Platform (MISP) as an external Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) source. Methods: The experimental evaluation is conducted using the AIT-ADS dataset, which consists of synthetic Wazuh alerts. Alerts produced by Wazuh are preprocessed, clustered using DBSCAN to separate normal density structures from anomalous traffic, and classified using Random Forest before being cross-checked against MISP indicators of compromise. Results: The experimental results show that the proposed pipeline achieved an overall accuracy of 99.76% and a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.9988 for binary threat classification, while reducing false positives by 66.78% and, after MISP enrichment, reducing false negatives by 66%. Conclusion: These results indicate that combining clustering-based anomaly detection, supervised classification, and external threat-intelligence enrichment can substantially reduce alert fatigue in security operations centers that rely on open-source SIEM platforms.

title: The Effect of SAP Implementation, System Integration, and User Competence on Project Performance Through Procurement Efficiency and Information Completeness at PT ADHI KARYA
abstractText: Background: Construction firms increasingly rely on integrated digital systems to coordinate procurement and project delivery. At PT ADHI KARYA (Persero) Tbk, however, the procurement workflow remains only partially integrated, even though SAP Materials Management (MM), SAP Project System (PS), and e-Procurement are already in use. Objective: This study examines the relationships of SAP Implementation, SAP–e-Procurement Integration, and User Competence with Project Performance, with Procurement Efficiency and Information Completeness specified as intervening mechanisms. Methods: Data were obtained from 100 purposively selected SAP users through an explanatory quantitative survey. The proposed measurement and structural models were evaluated using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Results: Procurement Efficiency was positively associated with SAP Implementation (β = 0.319; p = 0.007), SAP–e-Procurement Integration (β = 0.321; p = 0.002), and User Competence (β = 0.241; p = 0.014). Procurement Efficiency was also positively associated with Information Completeness (β = 0.500; p < 0.001) and Project Performance (β = 0.494; p < 0.001). Information Completeness showed an additional positive association with Project Performance (β = 0.530; p < 0.001). Bootstrap estimates of the indirect effects further supported the mediating roles of Procurement Efficiency and Information Completeness. Conclusion: Project performance is strengthened when SAP and e-Procurement operate as a more integrated workflow, procurement activities are executed efficiently, information is complete and reliable, and users possess the competence required to operate the systems effectively.
